# @moku-labs/game

> 2D puzzle game engine on TypeScript, built as a Layer-2 framework on @moku-labs/core. The game is a deterministic graph of business logic. State commits only on edges. Position is data. Player input and world events are answers a node waits for. The screen is a projection of committed state. V1 is the logic plugins `time`, `lifecycle`, `model`, `clock`, `flow` and a headless testing entry; V2 adds the screen plugins `world`, `renderer`, `input`, `assets`, `scenes`, a Pixi v8 renderer loaded lazily, and the `@moku-labs/game/assets` entry that generates typed asset keys. V3 adds the interface plugins `anim`, `i18n`, `text`, `ui` (`screen` lists all nine) and the opt-in `audio`: choreographies as data, strings as data, text from MSDF fonts, screens in JSX laid out by Yoga, sound as an effect a node awaits. V4 adds two doors for the editor: `@moku-labs/game/inspect` reads a running game, `@moku-labs/game/control` drives a dev build. V5 adds the opt-in plugin `effects`: particles and WGSL/GLSL filters as components. V6 adds the opt-in plugin `platform`: the Back button, haptics and keep-awake through a provider the game passes. The game shell makes a game a folder of data: `@moku-labs/game/app` (`defineGameApp`, `config.ts` as `GameConfig`), the page `@moku-labs/game/app/page`, the system shell `@moku-labs/game/app/system` and the bin `moku-game` that serves, builds, packages and packs the folder. The package is published on npm as `@moku-labs/game`, and this file ships inside it.

Facts: Bun only. ESM only. `"sideEffects"` lists the root entry `./dist/index.mjs` only, every other entry has none. `pixi.js` `^8.0.0` is a peer dependency, no V1 code imports it. `playwright-core` (visual tests), `sharp` (the asset pack), `typescript` (the project index), `@moku-labs/system` (the system shell and the store save) and `@moku-labs/native` (`moku-game native`) are optional peers. Node >= 24, Bun >= 1.4.2. TypeScript strict with `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` and `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`. The engine ships no genre rules: no merge, no match-3, no physics. A game brings its own pure rule functions.

## Entry points

- `@moku-labs/game`: everything a game imports.
- `@moku-labs/game/app`: `defineGameApp`, `startMoment` and the types of a game's `index.ts` and `config.ts`. No `node:` import, no system or native package. See "The game shell".
- `@moku-labs/game/app/page` (the browser): `startPage`, the page the generated `.moku/main.ts` calls.
- `@moku-labs/game/app/system` (the browser, the native shell): `systemShellOf`, `fromSystem`, `storeSave`, `createSystemApp`, the type `SystemModules`, over the optional peer `@moku-labs/system`. The one entry that names it, in types only: the page hands it the loaders.
- `@moku-labs/game/cli` (node and bun only): `runCli`, the bin `moku-game`, `preparePage`, the editor's dev page, `watchKeys`, the watch that keeps `generated/` fresh next to it, and `watchEngine`, the watch that tells when the installed engine changed.
- `@moku-labs/game/testing`: headless play, repro runs, isolated feature tests (`isolate`, `stub`), fake clock, the `fx` of a node for a unit test (`fakeFx`), in-memory save provider. No `node:` import.
- `@moku-labs/game/visual` (node and bun only): the visual tests `defineVisualTest`, `runVisualTests`, `parseVisualArgv`. The bin runs them: `moku-game visual`. A step is a `/control` command or `{ checkpoint: name, finish?: boolean }`: a checkpoint lands every motion before its snapshot, `finish: false` keeps them running (same frames in both legs). Both legs run on one clock: the pixel leg's dev page runs on a fake clock at the headless app's `clock.now()` (`startMoment`), standing still like the headless one.
- `@moku-labs/game/assets` (node and bun only): the asset key scanner, the production packer and the string compiler. The package bin `moku-game-assets` runs it.
- `@moku-labs/game/inspect`: the read door of the editor, safe in a production build. See "Doors for the editor".
- `@moku-labs/game/control`: the write door of the editor, dev builds only. See "Doors for the editor".
- `@moku-labs/game/hot` (the Bun dev server only): the Bun plugin that hot swaps views in a running page; `moku-game dev` lists it. See "Hot swap".
- `@moku-labs/game/lint`: the oxlint JS plugin `moku-game` with the game lint rules. See "Lint for games".
- `@moku-labs/game/project` (node and bun only): the project index, where every engine id of a game is defined, line read fresh at the call. It follows the tsconfig `paths` of the game. The package bin `moku-game-index` runs it. See "Project index".
- `@moku-labs/game/fonts/*`: the shipped MSDF body font and its licence. See "Fonts".
- `@moku-labs/game/jsx-runtime` and `@moku-labs/game/jsx-dev-runtime`: what `"jsxImportSource": "@moku-labs/game"` resolves to. A game never imports them by hand.

Root exports:
- Functions: `createApp`, `createPlugin`, `defineGame`, `defineFeature`, `flattenFeatures`, `type`, `exit`, `to`, `slot`, `contribution`, `schedule`, `guide`, `hint`, `defineEffect`.
- Class: `SaveUnreadableError`.
- Plugin instances: `timePlugin`, `lifecyclePlugin`, `modelPlugin`, `clockPlugin`, `flowPlugin`, `worldPlugin`, `rendererPlugin`, `inputPlugin`, `assetsPlugin`, `scenesPlugin`, `animPlugin`, `i18nPlugin`, `textPlugin`, `uiPlugin`, `audioPlugin`, `effectsPlugin`, `platformPlugin`; the list `screen` = `world`, `renderer`, `input`, `assets`, `scenes`, `anim`, `i18n`, `text`, `ui`. `effects`, `audio` and `platform` are opt-in: `plugins: [...screen, effectsPlugin, audioPlugin, platformPlugin]`, `platform` last.
- Screen helpers from the root: `component`, `tag`, `resource`, `mut`, `system`, `projection`, `Layer`, `Order`, `Exiting`, `Tree`, `Now`, `Transform`, `Sprite`, `NineSlice`, `Shape`, `Parent`, `Display`, `Overlay`, `HudPart`, `sprite`, `Tappable`, `Pressable`, `Draggable`, `DropTarget`, `Swipeable`, `Traceable`, `Touchable`, `Held`, `Hovered`, `PointerOver`, `Pressed`, `Pointer`, `Traced`, `defineBundles`, `load`, `defineScene`.
- Interface helpers from the root (V3): `defineAnimation`, `sequence`, `parallel`, `stagger`, `tween`, `set`, `wait`, `mark`, `frames`, `sfx`, `haptic`, `use`, `spawn`, `spawned`, `play`, `external`, `defineMotion`, `Animation`, `Frames`, the resource `AnimPlayer`; `tr`, `messageArgument`, `messageDuration`; `Text`, `label`, `defineTextStyles`, `bind`, `Countdown` and the types `BindOptions`, `CountdownValue`, `TextFormat`; `defineComponent`, `popup`, `defineStyle`, `defineTokens`, `resolve`, `Box`, `LocalWrite`, `DebugTrigger`, `ScrollState`; `music`. Also `stopSfx(id, { fadeMs? })` (ends a named sound, see audio) and `cubicBezier(x1, y1, x2, y2)` (a CSS-style easing curve for `tween`'s `ease`).
- Effects helpers from the root (V5): `defineEmitter`, `Emitter`, `defineFilter`, `Glow`, `Outline`, `Blur`, `ColorMatrix`, `Noise`, `Displacement`, `Alpha`.
- Platform from the root (V6): the types `PlatformProvider`, `BackResult`, `HapticKind` and the frozen list `HAPTIC_KINDS`.
- `defineGame<Types>()` returns, typed by the game's `player`, `session`, `assets`, `bundles`, `scenes`, `strings` and `textStyles`: `defineNode`, `defineFlow`, `defineFeature`, `projection`, `sprite`, `Sprite`, `NineSlice`, `defineBundles`, `load`, `defineScene`, `defineAnimation`, `frames`, `sfx`, `play`, `tr`, `label`, `defineTextStyles`, `defineComponent`, `defineStyle`, `defineTokens`, `popup`, `music`, `Frames`, `defineEmitter`, `Emitter`, `Displacement`, and `system` (its `ctx.snapshot` typed by `player` and `session`), `volumes` (the `audio` config's reader of the typed player), `key` (string keys from data, below). `Types` is `{ player; session; assets: string; bundles?: string; scenes?: string; strings: Record<string, unknown>; textStyles?: string; emitters?: string }`.
- `@moku-labs/game/assets`: `scanAssets(options)`, `emitKeys`, `emitManifest`, `compileStrings(root, out, options?)`, `checkStrings`, `packAssets(options)`, `exportStrings`, `importStrings`, `runCli(argv, strings)` with `strings: StringsTools` = `{ compile: compileStrings, exportStrings, importStrings }`. Audio files are `.mp3` or `.m4a`. Asset key = feature (or layer name) + "." + path inside `assets/`; a sub-feature's own name, `features/episodes/ep01/assets/ward/room.png` → `ep01.ward.room`. `runCli` (a game's `bun run assets:keys`) scans the assets and compiles the `strings/<locale>.json` of every feature and sub-feature, and the `strings/` of every layer, into `generated/strings.ts` (the `Strings` type for `defineGame`), one `generated/strings.<locale>.ts` per locale for the top-level features and the layers, and `generated/strings.<feature>.<locale>.ts` per sub-feature with string files, its keys only, each starting with `<feature>.` (it imports `messageArgument` and `messageDuration` from `@moku-labs/game` when a message needs them, no helper is copied in); `--check` fails when any output is out of date; `--pack <dir>` writes the production build. `--layer <folder>[=<name>]`, repeatable and good with every mode, scans `<root>/<folder>/` like one more feature under `<name>` (`<folder>` alone maps to itself): its `assets.ts`, `assets/` and `strings/<locale>.json`. A game on the layered layout passes `--layer shared=ui`, so `shared/assets/*` keeps the `ui.*` keys. A missing layer folder is a warning. `scanAssets`, `compileStrings`, `exportStrings` and `importStrings` take the same map as `layers: { shared: "ui" }`. `--pseudo` also writes the pseudo-locale `en-XA`. `--export <dir>` and `--import <dir>` exchange strings with translators; `--source <locale>` names the locale they read from, `"en"` by default. The package bin `moku-game-assets` is this CLI: a script is `"assets:keys": "moku-game-assets --root src --manifest public/assets/manifest.json --keys src/generated/assets.ts"`. A game with `config.ts` runs `moku-game keys` and `moku-game pack` instead: they pass its paths and its layers.
- Type namespaces: `Time`, `Lifecycle`, `Model`, `Clock`, `Flow`, `World`, `Renderer`, `Input`, `Assets`, `Scenes`, `Anim`, `I18n`, `TextTypes`, `Ui`, `Audio`, `Effects`, `Platform`. Use `import type { Flow } from "@moku-labs/game"` and then `Flow.RouteStep`, `Flow.NodeContext`, `Model.Json`, `Model.PlayerStateProvider`, `Clock.ClockSource`, `Time.Phase`, `Lifecycle.PauseReason`, `Anim.Target`, `I18n.Message`. `Text` is the component, so the text types are `TextTypes`.
- `defineNode` and `defineFlow` are NOT root exports. They come from `defineGame<Types>()`.

## Concepts

- Node: a small function with a plain `await` body. It gets one context object and returns `out.<outcome>(payload)`. A bare string is not accepted.
- Flow: an id, a `nodes` table, a `start` node and an `edges` table. One entry per outcome of every node. The compiler checks the table.
- Exactly one node is active. The runner opens one model transaction per node run and commits it on the edge. A node that throws changes nothing.
- Transit node: has `run`, no `rest`. Rest node: `rest: true`. The graph waits there. Without `run` it is a pure wait.
- A pure wait ends in two ways. A gate answer whose `intent` is an outcome name: the answer payload becomes the outcome payload. Or a world event whose `type` is listed in the node's `inbox`: the event payload becomes the outcome payload.
- Transition: rest node to rest node. It is a transaction. On an error the runner discards, rolls back to the last rest point, retries `retries` times, then enters `safeNode`. A failure inside `safeNode` rejects `run()`.
- Three ways to run an effect in a node. `await fx(descriptor)`: the node waits for it. `fx.start(descriptor)`: it starts now and the node goes on; write it in place of `void fx(...)`. A failure of a started effect is the log entry `flow:fx-start-failed` and never fails the node. A `cosmetic` descriptor (`sfx`, `play`, `haptic`, `music`) that fails, awaited or started, is the warn entry `flow:fx-cosmetic-failed` with `{ kind, message }` and resolves `undefined`; a descriptor with `answers` and a `guide` are refused, they have to be awaited. `fx.emit(hint(...))`: released after the commit of the edge, dropped in fast mode.
- `await fx(descriptor)` is typed by the descriptor (`Flow.Descriptor<Result>`): `schedule`, `guide`, `music`, `sfx`, `haptic`, `play` resolve `void`; `load` resolves `Assets.LoadResult | undefined` (`undefined` without `assets`, as in `game.headless()`); `ready` resolves `boolean | undefined` (`true` when every bundle is loaded and on the GPU, `undefined` without `assets`, so compare `=== false`); `popup(Component, props)` resolves `Flow.Answer<outcome names>`, so comparing it with an intent the component does not declare is a compile error; a descriptor written by hand resolves `unknown`. A game declares its own: `const envRead = defineEffect<{ notice: boolean }, EnvRead>("view-env.read", { fast: "run" })`, then `await fx(envRead({ notice: true }))` is `EnvRead` and `envRead.handle(ctx.require(flowPlugin).fx, payload => ...)` registers the one handler (returns the remover). Only `{ fast: "run" }` without `cosmetic` resolves `Result`; any other declaration resolves `Result | undefined`. `NodeFx` is generic: a hand-written fake is typed `as NodeFx`, or use `fakeFx`.
- Every failure is written into the log by the engine: an `error` entry `flow:error` with `{ path, rolledBackTo, retry, error: { message, stack } }`. Read it with `app.log.trace()`. A game needs no plugin for it.
- `recover` on a rest node: `recover: async ({ player, session, rng, fx, signal, now }) => { ... }`. It runs only when the runner gave up on a transition and enters this node as `safeNode`, before the node is entered. The rollback left the state of the failed rest point; `recover` writes the drafts so the safe node can draw itself. What it wrote commits as one edge with `outcome: "recover"` and becomes the rest point. A `recover` that throws rejects `run()`. A retry does not run it. So the safe node stays a pure wait: no `run` body, no extra outcome, no self edge.
- Entering a rest node calls `model.store.markRest()`: the save provider gets the patches. Leaving a `barrier` node calls `markBarrier(txId)`: a durable write, and rollback cannot cross it.
- `checkpoint: true` on a rest node: the journal is compacted there. `safeNode` must be a checkpoint.
- The gate keeps an answer it refused while closed and offers it once to the next gate that opens. Config `flow.holdMs`, in milliseconds of game time: `0` (default) keeps it for one frame and the first answer wins; above `0` the last answer wins and it is dropped when older than `holdMs`; `Infinity` keeps it until the next gate opens. Set it above the longest transit animation a tap should survive. A gate that does not list the intent drops it. Nothing is kept in a fast walk or while time does not run. A held answer is dropped when the runner gives up and enters `safeNode`, when a bookmark is entered and when the graph stops. The gate keeps one answer, never a queue; for a flight that must not close the gate, commit at once and `fx.start(play(...))`, or draw the flight from state with a `change` hook.
- `over: true`: entering the node waits while a pointer is down.
- Path: node names joined by `/` through sub-flows and slots. Examples: `"home"`, `"board/awaitIntent"`, `"afterBonus/thanks"`.
- Edge target: a node name, `exit(...)` or `to(...)`. A payload must fit the input of the target. A node without input accepts any payload.
- Sub-flow: a flow that declares `outcomes` is used as a node of another flow. `exit("name")` leaves it with that outcome.
- Slot: `slot("name")` is a node with the outcome `done`; `slot("name", { shop: type<{ tab: string }>() })` declares more outcomes (never `done`), and the flow that holds the slot gives each an edge, as for a node. Features contribute sub-flows to it. They run in `order`. `when(snapshot)` can skip one; it always reads the committed state, also what an earlier contribution of the same slot wrote. A contribution may hold a slot of its own. A contribution that exits `done` hands over to the next one, and the slot ends with its own `done` edge after the last. A contribution that exits an outcome the slot declares leaves the slot at once with its payload: the later contributions do not run, and the slot takes its own edge of that outcome (a journal entry and a `flow:edge`, like `done`). The next entry of a slot starts at its first contribution. `contribution(slot, { flow, order, when? })` builds the `contribute` entry and checks at compile time that every outcome of the flow is `done` or a declared outcome whose payload fits. `run()` refuses a contribution of a slot with declared outcomes that declares another outcome, and one slot name declared with different outcomes; it warns about named exits into a slot that declares none, and about two contributions without `when` in a slot that declares some. A slot never counts as a rest node: more than `max(64, 4 × n)` edges without one fail the node, `n` being the nodes of the graph expanded from the main flow (a sub-flow once per entry that uses it, a slot with all its contributions).
- Feature: `defineFeature(name, description)` makes an ordinary plugin that registers into `flow.features` in `onInit`. Pass it in `createApp({ plugins: [...] })`. `feature.logicOnly` is the same plugin with the V1 keys only, for headless tests. `features: [episodesKitFeature, ep01Feature, ep02Feature]` declares sub-features, each in a folder of its own inside the parent's (`features/episodes/ep01/`); `flattenFeatures([homeFeature, episodesFeature])` gives the flat plugin list, a parent before its children, depth first, and a parent's `onInit` throws when a declared sub-feature is not composed. `flow.features.all()` gives `{ name, description, parent? }` per feature.
- Modes: `"live"` and `"fast"`. In fast mode effects answer instantly, hints are dropped and only `runInFast` handlers run. All node logic runs for real.

## Authoring helpers, with signatures

```ts
function defineGame<Types extends Flow.GameTypes>();  // returns the helpers listed under "Root exports", typed by Types
// GameTypes = { player: Json; session: Json; assets: string; strings: Record<string, unknown>;
//               bundles?: string; scenes?: string; textStyles?: string; emitters?: string }

function type<Payload = void>(): TypeTag<Payload>;

// From the kit. Input and Tags are inferred from the spec.
defineNode(spec: {
  input?: TypeTag<Input>;
  outcomes: Tags;                      // { done: type(), failed: type<{ reason: string }>() }
  rest?: boolean;                      // run is required unless rest: true
  over?: boolean;
  checkpoint?: boolean;
  barrier?: boolean;
  inbox?: readonly (keyof Tags & string)[];
  run?: (ctx: NodeContext) => Result | Promise<Result>;
  guide?: (state: { player; session }) => GuideOptions | undefined;  // the tutorial step derived from committed state, see "Tutorial guide"
}): NodeDefinition;

defineFlow(id: string, spec: {
  nodes: Nodes;                        // node, sub-flow or slot per name
  start: string;                       // a node whose input accepts the flow input
  edges: Table;                        // edges[node][outcome] = target
  input?: TypeTag<Input>;
  outcomes?: FlowTags;                 // declare them to use the flow as a node
}): FlowDefinition;

function exit<const Name extends string>(outcome: Name): Exit<Name>;
function to<const TargetName extends string, Payload, Output>(
  target: TargetName,
  map: (payload: Payload) => Output    // annotate the parameter type yourself
): Mapped<TargetName, Payload, Output>;
function slot<const Name extends string, const Tags extends OutcomeTags = Record<never, never>>(
  name: Name,
  outcomes?: Tags                      // { shop: type<{ tab: string }>() }; declaring done throws a TypeError
): SlotNode<Tags, Name>;               // outcomes: done, then the declared ones
function contribution<S extends SlotNode<OutcomeTags, string>, F extends AnyFlow>(
  slot: S,
  spec: { flow: F; order: number; when?: (snapshot: Snapshot) => boolean }
): Readonly<Record<S["name"], ContributionSpec>>;   // { [slot.name]: { flow, order, when? } }
// contribute: { ...contribution(episodeStep, { flow: storyFlow, order: 10 }) }
// compile error when storyFlow declares an outcome episodeStep does not declare, or its payload does not fit

function defineFeature(name: string, description: FeatureDescription): FeaturePlugin;
// FeatureDescription = {
//   nodes?: readonly AnyNode[];
//   flows?: readonly AnyFlow[];
//   contribute?: Record<string, ContributionSpec>;            // ContributionSpec = { flow: AnyFlow; order: number; when?: (snapshot: Snapshot) => boolean }
//   features?: readonly FeaturePlugin[];                       // sub-features, composed right after this one
//   projections?, systems?, components?, scenes?, assets?;   // V2 keys, read by world, scenes and assets
//   systemsRun?: never;                                        // the 0.15.3 key, removed: a system runs while its query has an entity
//   animations?: readonly AnimationDefinition[];              // V3, read by anim
//   ui?: readonly ComponentDefinition[];                      // V3, read by ui (defineComponent results)
//   strings?: Record<locale, CompiledMessages | (() => Promise<unknown>)>;   // V3, read by i18n
//   textStyles?: ReturnType<typeof defineTextStyles>;         // V3, read by text
//   emitters?: readonly ReturnType<typeof defineEmitter>[];   // V5, read by effects
//   filters?: readonly ReturnType<typeof defineFilter>[];     // V5, read by effects
// }

function schedule(moment: number | undefined): Descriptor;  // awaited, asks the clock for one `elapsed`
function guide(options: GuideOptions): Descriptor;          // awaited, narrows the gate to one answer
function hint(kind: string, payload?: Json): Hint;          // for fx.emit, cosmetic
// GuideOptions = { allow: { intent: string; payload?: Json }; target?: AnchorTarget | readonly AnchorTarget[];
//                  pad?: number; veil?: { color?: number; alpha?: number } | false; blocked?: { intent: string; payload?: Json };
//                  highlight?, hand?, text? (deprecated: not drawn by the engine, draw them in an <anchor>) }
// Descriptor   = { kind: string; payload?: Json; answers?: readonly string[]; cosmetic?: boolean }
```

## Node context

```ts
type NodeContext = {
  input: Input;          // payload of the edge that led here
  player: Player;        // draft of the saved player tree, mutate it
  session: Session;      // draft of the session tree, never saved
  rng: RngView;          // rng.stream(id) gives a deterministic stream
  fx: NodeFx;            // await fx(descriptor), fx.start(descriptor), fx.emit(hint(...))
  out: Out;              // one method per declared outcome
  signal: AbortSignal;   // aborted on stop, restore and inbox delivery
  now: number;           // clock.now() read once at node entry
};
```

`RngStream` methods, integers only: `int(maxExclusive)`, `range(min, maxInclusive)`, `pick(items)`, `weighted(table)` with `{ weight: number }` entries, `chance(numerator, denominator)`.

## Rules of determinism

- Never call `Date.now()`, `performance.now()` or `new Date()` in a node or in rule functions. Use `now` from the node context.
- Never call `Math.random()`. Use `rng.stream("some-id")`. Use one id per source, for example `"chest:42"`. Stream state is part of the save, so a draw commits and rolls back with its transaction.
- Never call `setTimeout` or `setInterval` in game logic. Store the due moment in `player`, then `await fx(schedule(moment))` and wait for `elapsed` at a rest node with `inbox: ["elapsed"]`.
- State is plain JSON only. No classes, no `Map`, no `Date`, no `undefined` values in trees.
- Change state only through `player` and `session` of the node context. Do not keep game state in module scope or closures.
- Keep rules as pure functions `(state, input, tables) => result`. The node calls the rule and writes the result into the draft.
- A node never calls `app.model`, `app.clock` or `app.time`. Everything outside logic goes through `fx`.
- A timer is a moment stored in player state. How long is left is computed from `now`.

## Lint for games

`.oxlintrc.json` of a game (oxlint 1.86.0 or later). The engine ships no default severity: a game turns each rule on.

```json
{
  "jsPlugins": ["@moku-labs/game/lint"],
  "rules": {
    "moku-game/lazy-imports": "error",
    "moku-game/native-imports": "error",
    "moku-game/dev-imports": "error",
    "moku-game/no-module-state": "error",
    "moku-game/determinism": "error",
    "moku-game/rules-siblings": "error",
    "moku-game/static-keys": "error",
    "moku-game/layer-imports": "error",
    "moku-game/feature-door": "error",
    "moku-game/sub-features": "error",
    "moku-game/test-suffix": "error"
  }
}
```

- `moku-game/lazy-imports` (L2): no static value import of `pixi.js` or `yoga-layout`. `import type` and `import()` pass. Default files `**`.
- `moku-game/native-imports` (L13): no `@moku-labs/system`, `@moku-labs/native`, `@tauri-apps/*` in the logic, the root `index.ts` and `config.ts`, `kit.ts` and `plugins/`. A game imports no native package: it names the capability in `config.ts` `system`, and the engine page wires it.
- `moku-game/dev-imports`: `@moku-labs/editor` and `@moku-labs/game/control` only in `*.dev.ts(x)`, tests and the generated `.moku/` page (and `web/main.ts`, `web/dev*.ts`, `web/editor*.ts` of a game that still has `web/`).
- `moku-game/no-module-state` (L5): no module-scope `let` or `var`, no module-scope `new Map/Set/WeakMap/WeakSet`. Default files `**`.
- `moku-game/determinism` (L3): no `Math.random`, `Date.now`, `performance.now`, `new Date()`, `setTimeout`, `setInterval` in the logic. `new Date(now)` passes. Plugin folders, `**/{plugin,plugins}/**`, are the effect side and are skipped: a plugin answers `schedule` with a timer.
- `moku-game/rules-siblings` (L4): a file under `rules/` imports only `./` siblings, `@core/types` and `@shared/rules`, by alias or by relative path. `@core/kit`, `../tables` and `import type … from "@moku-labs/game"` are reported.
- `moku-game/static-keys`: a JSX `key` is a literal, a template of such parts, `props.id` or `props.<name>Key`, a call, or a `const` of one. `tabKeys[props.tab]`, `a ?? b`, `a || b`, `a ? b : c` and `props.tab` are reported: pass the key in as a prop, `<TabButton id="tabSound" />`. Default files `**/*.tsx`.
- `moku-game/layer-imports`: the order is core ← shared ← features ← `game.ts`; plugins import core and shared; every layer may import `generated/`. An import, export-from or `import()` that reaches a layer above its own is reported, `import type` too: `@features/home` from `shared/`. Only `game.ts` imports `game.ts`.
- `moku-game/feature-door`: another feature is imported only through its `index.ts`, `@features/orders`, never `@features/orders/flow/merge`. Only `game.ts` imports the barrels `@features` and `@plugins`. A feature does not import its own `index.ts`. A relative import that leaves the feature is written as an alias: `@features/<f>`, `@shared`, `@core/<file>`. Inside one feature any relative import passes. At any depth: the unit of a file is the deepest feature unit that holds it, a feature owner (a folder of `features/`, or a folder inside an owner with a door `index.ts` and `assets/`, `assets.ts` or `strings/` of its own) or a code-only sub-feature its parent's door imports from `./<folder>` and lists in `features: [...]`. A sub-feature never imports a feature it lives in, door or file, by alias or by path: `Door: a sub-feature does not import the feature it lives in: features/episodes/ep01 imports features/episodes. Move what they share into a sibling sub-feature, such as features/episodes/episodes-kit, and import it from its door.` A parent reaches a child's door by `./ep01` from its door, `../ep01` from its own files, or by alias; a sibling only by alias, `@features/episodes/episodes-kit`. A flat game lints as before: a folder with an `index.ts` that no door lists in `features: [...]` stays part of its feature.
- `moku-game/sub-features`: the door of a feature imports every sub-feature owner from `./<folder>` and lists it in `features: [...]`, lists only names imported from a sub-feature folder (a child folder with a door, not a kind folder), and the door of a sub-feature, owner or code-only, registers a feature named like its folder: a call whose first argument is the literal folder name passes, so a factory such as `defineEpisode("ep03", { … })` does too. A code-only sub-feature declares no sub-features of its own. Default files `**/features/**/index.{ts,tsx}`; options as the layout rules. A flat game reports nothing.
- `moku-game/test-suffix`: a file in a test kind folder ends with its suffix. `tests/e2e/` `.e2e.ts`, `tests/visual/` `.visual.ts`, `tests/editor/` `.editor.ts`, `__tests__/`, `__tests__/unit/` and `__tests__/integration/` `.test.ts`, `__tests__/isolated/` `.isolated.ts`, `__tests__/visual/` `.visual.ts`; a `.tsx` file adds an `x`. An `index.ts` of a kind folder passes, such as `tests/visual/index.ts` of `moku-game visual`. Helpers go to `tests/helpers/` or `__tests__/fixtures/`.
- Layers under the game root: `core/**`, `shared/**`, `features/<f>/**` and `features/<f>/<sub>/**`, `plugins/<p>/**`, `generated/**`, `game.ts`, `tests/**`. A file outside them (`kit.ts`, `nodes/`, `web/`) keeps the layout rules quiet, so a game on the template layout lints as before.
- Aliases: `layer-imports`, `feature-door` and `rules-siblings` read the `compilerOptions.paths` of `tsconfig.json` (comments, trailing commas and relative `extends` included), the way the project index does. Without `paths` they read the v15 table: `@core/*` → `core/*`, `@shared` → `shared/index.ts`, `@shared/rules` → `shared/rules/index.ts`, `@features` → `features/index.ts`, `@features/*` → `features/*/index.ts`, `@plugins` → `plugins/index.ts`, `@generated/*` → `generated/*`, `@tests/*` → `tests/*`. `aliasTargetsOf(tsconfig, root, specifier)` from `@moku-labs/game/lint` answers what they read: for a game without a tsconfig, `aliasTargetsOf("/game/tsconfig.json", "/game", "@features/orders")` is `["/game/features/orders/index.ts"]`. The `*` of `@features/*` crosses `/`: `@features/episodes/ep01` is the door of the sub-feature, `features/episodes/ep01/index.ts`.
- Logic = the root `index.ts`, `**/state.ts`, `**/tables.ts`, `**/game.ts`, `**/{core,nodes,flows,rules,features,shared}/**`. Tests (`tests/**`, `**/__tests__/**`, `*.test.ts`) are skipped by every rule but `test-suffix`.
- Every rule takes `["error", { "files": [...], "ignores": [...] }]`. Globs are relative to the directory oxlint runs in; a key given replaces the default. `layer-imports`, `feature-door`, `sub-features` and `rules-siblings` also take `root` (the folder of `core/`, `shared/`, `features/`, `plugins/` and `game.ts`, default `.`) and `tsconfig` (default `tsconfig.json`); `test-suffix` takes `root` and `suffixes` (kind folder to suffix, replaces the table whole).

## Minimal game

```ts
// state.ts
import { defineGame } from "@moku-labs/game";

export type Player = { coins: number; lastRoll: number };
export type Session = { rolls: number };

export const { defineNode, defineFlow, defineFeature } = defineGame<{
  player: Player;
  session: Session;
  assets: string;
  strings: Record<string, unknown>;
}>();
```

```ts
// nodes.ts
import { type } from "@moku-labs/game";
import { defineNode } from "./state";

export const home = defineNode({
  outcomes: { roll: type() },
  rest: true,
  checkpoint: true
});

export const roll = defineNode({
  outcomes: { done: type() },
  run: ({ player, session, rng, out }) => {
    const face = rng.stream("dice").range(1, 6);

    player.coins += face;
    player.lastRoll = face;
    session.rolls += 1;
    return out.done();
  }
});
```

```ts
// flow.ts
import { defineFlow } from "./state";
import { home, roll } from "./nodes";

export const mainFlow = defineFlow("main", {
  nodes: { home, roll },
  start: "home",
  edges: {
    home: { roll: "roll" },
    roll: { done: "home" }
  }
});
```

```ts
// index.ts: the game as one data object
import { defineGameApp } from "@moku-labs/game/app";
import { mainFlow } from "./flow";

export default defineGameApp({
  flow: mainFlow,
  safeNode: "home",
  player: { coins: 0, lastRoll: 0 },
  session: { rolls: 0 }
});
```

```ts
// config.ts: the page, as plain data
import type { GameConfig } from "@moku-labs/game/app";

export default { page: { title: "Dice" } } satisfies GameConfig;
```

The game never calls `flow.run()`. The page runs the graph after `app.start()`; a test hands the app to `createHeadless`, which runs it. The screen sends answers with `app.flow.gate.answer({ intent: "roll" })`.

## The game shell

A game is a folder: `index.ts` (`export default defineGameApp({ ... })`), `config.ts` (plain data, `satisfies GameConfig`), `core/`, `shared/`, `features/` (features, and inside a feature its sub-features: `features/<parent>/<child>/`), `plugins/`, `generated/`, `tests/` with `tests/scenarios/<name>.ts`. No `web/`, no `native.ts`, no `platform-bridge.ts`, no `bunfig.toml`, no `createApp` call. `.moku/` holds what `moku-game` writes; the game's `.gitignore` lists it. Scripts of the game's `package.json`: `"dev": "moku-game dev"`, `"build": "moku-game build"`, `"native:ios-sim": "moku-game native build ios --simulator"`.

- `defineGameApp(definition)` returns the game, `{ headless(seams?), screen(seams?) }`, and creates no app. Every type comes from the object; no generic at the call site. Keys: `flow` (required), `safeNode` (default: the start of the main flow), `player` and `session` (required), `orientation` (`"portrait"`), `referenceSide` (1080), `referenceLong` (1920), `seed` (42), `shared` (composed first among the features), `features` (the top-level features only: a parent brings the sub-features it declares, and the shell composes the tree depth first, a parent before its children), `plugins` (their APIs land on `screen().app`), `headless: { features?, plugins? }` (`features` left out takes the game's `features`, `[]` means none, `shared` is not composed; flattened the same way, and it may name a sub-feature alone), `pluginConfigs`.
- `pluginConfigs` takes every plugin of the screen app but the keys the shell writes. A seam-owned key is a compile error: `model.playerProvider`, `initialPlayer`, `initialSession`, `seed` (the game keeps `schemaVersion`, `migrations`); all of `clock` and `platform`; `flow.mainFlow`, `safeNode`; `renderer.mount`; `assets.manifest`, `io`; `audio.context`.
- `game.headless(seams?)` composes the core plugins, `logicOnly` of `headless.features` (of `features` when left out), then `headless.plugins`. `game.screen(seams?)` composes the screen set, `audio`, `effects`, `platform`, then `shared`, the features with their sub-features and the game's plugins; `[homeFeature, episodesFeature]` composes `home`, `episodes`, `episodes-kit`, `ep01`, `ep02`. Both return `{ app, clock, provider }`, the app not started; each call is fresh. Defaults: `fakeClock(startMoment)` (`startMoment` is `1_000_000`), a fresh `memory()` save, the seed of the definition or 42.
- Seams of both: `seed`, `clock`, `provider`, `player`, `session`. Screen only: `manifest` (a URL or the parsed file), `io`, `platform`, `keepAwake` (false), `audio: { context?, journal? }`, `renderer: { mount?, loadPixi?, preference? }`. Without a mount the renderer is inert, so `game.screen()` runs in plain Bun.
- `defineGameApp` throws `[game] defineGameApp needs flow.` and `[game] defineGameApp: features[2] is not a feature.` (at any depth: `features[1].features[0]`) for what TypeScript cannot stop. A feature in the tree twice, listed by the game and by its parent, or by two parents, is `[game] defineGameApp: the feature "ep01" is listed twice: features[1].features[1] and features[2].`; a `shared` with sub-features is `[game] defineGameApp: shared declares sub-features.`
- A game's exit plugin calls `ctx.require(platformPlugin).exit()` itself.

```ts
// a test of the dice game
import { startMoment } from "@moku-labs/game/app";
import { createHeadless } from "@moku-labs/game/testing";
import game from "./index";

const { app, clock, provider } = game.headless();
const run = await createHeadless(app);

run.state().path; // "home"
clock.now() === startMoment; // true
provider.calls.map(call => call.method); // ["load", "commit"]: a new player
await run.walk([{ at: "home", intent: "roll" }, { at: "home", intent: "roll" }]);
app.model.store.snapshot().session; // { rolls: 2 }
await run.stop();
```

`config.ts` keys and defaults: `page.title` (required, never empty), `page.lang` (`"en"`), `page.background` (`"#000000"`: the page behind the canvas, the `theme-color` meta and the native window; the canvas clear colour stays `pluginConfigs.renderer.background`), `page.orientation` (`"portrait"`, or `"landscape"`, `"any"`: the native build locks it), `page.icons: { favicon?, appleTouch? }` (files relative to the game, `<link>` tags), `page.head` (raw tags, verbatim), `page.boot: { image, width?, fadeMs? }` (absent by default; an `<img id="moku-boot">` centred over the canvas from the first paint until the first scene drew, then faded over `fadeMs`, `300`, and removed; `image` a file relative to the game, `width` `"40vmin"`), `native: { name, identifier, icon?, targets?, signing?, ios?, dev? }` (absent: no native build; `signing.android: { keystorePath, keystorePasswordEnv, keyPasswordEnv?, keyAlias }`, the path absolute, `~/...` or relative to the game, the passwords by env var name only; `signing.apple: { teamId }`; `ios: { minimumVersion?, infoPlist?, privacyManifest? }`, the minimum `"26.0"` by default, `infoPlist` of `PlistValue`: strings, booleans, arrays, dictionaries, a number or `null` refused; the manifest relative to the game; `dev: { identifier, name?, icon? }`, the test app of `--store --dev`, the identifier ending in `.dev` and not `native.identifier`, `name` `"<name> DEV"` and `icon` `native.icon` by default), `system` (`[]`; names `lifecycle`, `back`, `haptics`, `keepAwake`, `store`), `save` (`"memory"`, or `"local"`, `"store"`), `assets.layers` (`{}`; `{ shared: "ui" }` becomes `--layer shared=ui`), `debug.overlay` (`"closed"`, or `"pill"`, `"open"`: how the editor's overlay shows when a debug page starts; the page calls `app.debug.overlay.open({ mode })` right after the agents started; only a page with the agent reads it). A refused value throws, for example `[game] config.save is "disk".` or `[game] config.system names "tray", which the game shell does not wire.`

```ts
// config.ts of a game in a native shell
import type { GameConfig } from "@moku-labs/game/app";

export default {
  page: { title: "Лесной городок", lang: "ru", background: "#10161d", orientation: "portrait", icons: { favicon: "assets/icon.png" } },
  native: { name: "Лесной городок", identifier: "com.mokulabs.timber", icon: "assets/icon.png" },
  system: ["lifecycle", "back", "haptics", "keepAwake"],
  save: "memory",
  assets: { layers: { shared: "ui" } }
} satisfies GameConfig;
```

The page. `moku-game dev` and `build` write a `main.ts` that calls `startPage(game, config, { scenarios?, system?, agents?, devModules? })`. In order it resolves the config; picks the start; builds the system shell when the page has one and picks the save; makes `game.screen()` with the canvas on `#game`, `manifest.json` next to the page, the device clock and the shell's platform; sets `globalThis.game` (the app), `globalThis.system` (the system app or `undefined`) and `globalThis.doors` (`read`, `watch`, `sources`; `run`, `commands` in dev); follows reduced motion; starts the shell, the app, and runs the graph (a stop is logged `[game] The graph stopped.`); in dev starts the agents with `{ app, name, modules }`; last, on `pagehide` it flushes the save, and stops the app when the page is really left (`persisted` false); a page kept in the back/forward cache keeps its app running.
- `?player=<name>` starts from the scenario `tests/scenarios/<name>.ts` on a fresh memory save, never on the stored one. An unknown name logs `[game] No scenario "<name>".` and starts from the starting player. A scenario is `Scenario<Player>`: `(now) => ({ player, session? })`, its default export.
- `?renderer=webgl` asks Pixi for WebGL.
- Save kinds: `"memory"` lives for the page only; `"local"` is `localStorage` under `<native.identifier>:save` or `moku-game:save`, and falls back to memory with a warning where storage is refused; `"store"` is the system store (idb on the web, the Tauri store native), needs the shell, rejects a load it cannot read instead of starting a new player.
- System: the generated `main.ts` imports `systemShellOf` of `@moku-labs/game/app/system` only when `system` is not empty or `save` is `"store"`, so a web-only page bundles no system code. It passes `system: systemShellOf({ system: () => import("@moku-labs/system"), haptics: () => import("@moku-labs/system/haptics") })`: one loader per named plugin, in the order `lifecycle`, `back`, `haptics`, `keepAwake` (entry `keep-awake`), `store` (when named or `save` is `"store"`). The engine holds no `import()` of the package, so the page bundles only the named plugins: a game with `system: ["haptics"]` and a memory save builds without `@tauri-apps/plugin-store`. A loader that rejects: `[game] config.system needs @moku-labs/system.` with `bun add @moku-labs/system@^0.3.1`. A named plugin without a loader: `[game] config.system names "<name>", but main.ts has no loader for it.`

```ts
// .moku/main.ts of the engine's mini game, written by moku-game dev
// Written by moku-game dev. Do not edit.
import "./dev.ts";
import "./assets-stamp.ts";
import { startPage } from "@moku-labs/game/app/page";
import game from "../index.ts";
import config from "../config.ts";
import scenario0 from "../tests/scenarios/ready.ts";

await startPage(game, config, {
  scenarios: { "ready": scenario0 }
});
```

Commands of the bin `moku-game` (bun). Every command takes `--root <dir>` (default `.`), `--preload <path>` and `--serve-plugin <path>` (both repeat), before or after the command word. Exit 0 on success, else 1 with a `[game] …` line.
- `moku-game dev [--port 3000] [--packed]`: writes `.moku/index.html`, `script.ts` (the `moku:script` startup mark), `dev.ts` (sets `__MOKU_GAME_BUILD__` `"dev"`, the engine id `__MOKU_GAME_ENGINE__`, `__MOKU_GAME_CONTROL__`, `__MOKU_GAME_AGENT__` and last `__MOKU_GAME_DEV__`), `main.ts`, `assets-stamp.ts`, `bunfig.toml` (the hot plugin first, `__MOKU_GAME_DEV__`, `__MOKU_GAME_AGENT__` and `__MOKU_GAME_CONTROL__` defined `true`), runs Bun again under that bunfig in the game folder and serves `/`. It prints `› engine <id>` (and the patch file when there is one), then `› <folder>: dev server, raw assets. Ctrl+C stops it.` and then the bound URL alone on its own line, `http://localhost:3000/`. `--port 0` takes a free port. `--packed` serves `dist/assets`. A new or removed file in `tests/scenarios/` rewrites `main.ts`. On the raw files it keeps `generated/` fresh: it runs the scan of `keys` once before the page is written, and a save of an asset file (`.png`, `.webp`, `.fnt`, `.mp3`, `.m4a`) or of a `strings/<locale>.json` runs it again 100 ms after the last file event and prints `› keys: <path>` or `› keys: <path> and <n> more`; a folder that becomes or stops being a sub-feature (it gains or loses its door, `assets/`, `assets.ts` or `strings/`) scans too, `› keys: features/episodes/ep03/`; a changed or new string hot swaps through `generated/strings.<locale>.ts`, an asset file saved with new bytes swaps in the running page and a new or removed one reloads it, both through `.moku/assets-stamp.ts`, which `main.ts` imports (see "Hot swap"), and files answer `Cache-Control: no-store`. A failed scan is one warning `[game] keys: <message>` and the server runs on. A changed layer in `config.ts` needs a restart; `--packed` watches nothing. A taken port: `[game] dev: port 3000 is in use.` with `Pass --port 0 for a free port.` It watches the installed engine: 300 ms after a new version or dist it warns `[game] dev: the engine changed (<old id> -> <new id>), restarting the dev server.`, stops the child with SIGTERM, writes the page again with the new id and starts a new child (a fixed port keeps its URL, `--port 0` prints a new one); a patch file that changed while the engine did not is one warning that asks for `bun install`.
- `moku-game build [--out dist/web]`: packs the assets, bundles the page minified with `__MOKU_GAME_DEV__`, `__MOKU_GAME_AGENT__` and `__MOKU_GAME_CONTROL__` defined `false` (no scenario, no agent, no `.dev` module, no `/control`, no engine id), every link `./`, and copies the pack beside it with `manifest.json` next to `index.html`. Every page marks `moku:script` first and `moku:main` first after its imports. A release page whose `.js` carries `"/__editor/hello"` or `"[moku-editor]"` (the editor's agent) fails with `[game] build: the release page carries the editor agent (…)` and its output folder is removed. Runs from any http sub-path and from Tauri, not from `file://`.
- `moku-game build --debug[=read] [--editor host:port]`: a debug page, never shipped: the release page plus `@moku-labs/editor/agent/page` (resolved from the game, else `[game] build --debug needs @moku-labs/editor in the game.`) and the game's `.dev` modules, started after the app; DEV `false`, AGENT `true`, CONTROL `true` (`--debug`: every command, cheats too; `--debug=full` is an alias that prints one line) or `false` (`--debug=read`, the rare read-only page: read and cosmetic commands); `__MOKU_GAME_BUILD__` `debug-<UTC stamp>` for both, `__MOKU_GAME_ENGINE__` the engine id (`<version>+<dist hash>[.patch.<hash>]`, `+src` from sources), `__MOKU_GAME_EDITOR__` the `--editor` address (default `127.0.0.1:47600`); the title reads `<title> Debug`; no hot swap, no frame recorder, no audio journal, no scenario. It prints one warning naming the profile, the build id, the engine and the editor. `MOKU_NATIVE_PROFILE=store` with `--debug` is refused. `MOKU_NATIVE_PROFILE=dev`, a test app's web build: a run without `--debug` is refused (`[game] build: MOKU_NATIVE_PROFILE is dev: a dev page carries the overlay.`); `--debug` builds `__MOKU_GAME_EDITOR__` exactly `"off"`, so the agent opens no socket, with CONTROL `true` and `__MOKU_GAME_APP__` `native.dev.identifier`; `--editor`, `--debug=read` and an `@moku-labs/editor` below 0.10.19, or of a version that cannot be read, are refused.
- `moku-game native build <target> [--simulator] [--debug[=full] [--editor host:port]]`, `native dev <target>`, `native doctor [<target>]`, `native clean [<target>]`: one verb of `@moku-labs/native` (a dev dependency, `^0.3.13`) over `config.ts`. App name, identifier and icon from `native`, orientation and background colour from `page`; the web build is `moku-game build`, the dev server `moku-game dev --port 5173`; system rows for `back`, `haptics`, `store`; the Tauri project in `.moku/tauri`, the apps in `dist-native`; an Android app composes native's `shell` system first. `native build android --debug` builds a debug app (`debug: true` to native, which installs it beside the store app; the web build is `moku-game build --debug` with the same profile and `--editor`). `native build ios --debug [--simulator]` is the same app on iOS: the engine names it `<name> (debug)` and `<identifier>.debug`, in `.moku/tauri-debug`, native delivers to `dist-native/ios-debug`. Other verbs and targets refuse `--debug`. `native clean` also cleans `.moku/tauri-dev` and `.moku/tauri-debug` when they exist, one native clean per folder; `doctor` stays on `.moku/tauri`. `[game] config.ts has no native section.` without `native`.
- `moku-game native build <ios|android> --store --build-number <n>`: a store build, an `.aab` on Android (`aab: true` to native), an `.ipa` with `exportMethod: "app-store-connect"` on iOS. `app.version` from `package.json`, `app.buildNumber` from the flag, an integer from 1 to 2100000000, one number for both stores. Refused before `config.ts` is read: outside `native build`, with `--debug`, `--editor` or `--simulator`, on another target, without a valid number; `--build-number` without `--store`. Then every problem at once, before anything compiles, in one `[game] native --store: …` error, a line per problem: no signing block for the target, on Android a keystore that is not a file or an unset password variable (its name only, never a value), a `package.json` version that is not `x.y.z`, an identifier that ends in `.soak`, `.debug`, `.dev`, `.test` or `.staging`. On iOS it warns, and goes on, without `ios.privacyManifest` or `ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption` in `ios.infoPlist`. A build without `--store` runs no store check: `native build ios` is a device build. `--store --dev` builds the test app of `native.dev`: every store check, the identifier row reading `native.dev.identifier`; `dev: true` to native (`aab` on Android as before), the same signing, the web build `moku-game build --debug`, the project `.moku/tauri-dev`, a full Rust build of its own, the apps in `dist-native-dev`; the save stays under `native.identifier`. `--dev` without `--store` is refused before `config.ts` is read, with no `native.dev` right after, and `--store --debug` stays refused. Every build takes a valid `package.json` version (else native's `0.1.0`), `app.keepScreenOn` from `keepAwake` in `system`, and on iOS the minimum `26.0`; a debug app leaves `signing.android` out and keeps the SDK key.
- `moku-game keys [--check]`: `generated/assets.ts`, the compiled strings (`strings.ts`, `strings.<locale>.ts` for the top-level features and the layers, and `strings.<feature>.<locale>.ts` for every sub-feature with string files) and the dev manifest `generated/manifest.json` (a sub-feature's bundle carries its `dir` and `parent`); `dev` runs the same scan at start and on save and serves the manifest on `/manifest.json`, `visual` stops without it. `moku-game pack [--no-cache]`: `dist/assets`. Both pass the layers of `config.ts`.
- `moku-game visual [--update] [--only <name>] [--no-pixels | --pixels] [--webgl] [--dir <path>] [--tests <file>] [--url <url>]`: runs `runVisualTests` with the default export of `tests/visual/index.ts`, `{ app, tests }` (`app` is a `VisualSetup` `{ app, page? }`: `export default { app: { app: fixtureApp }, tests }`), against `tests/visual/baselines/`. The flags go through `parseVisualArgv`. The pixel leg runs on a Mac only unless `--pixels`/`--no-pixels`; without `--url` the command writes its own page into `.moku/visual/` (the page of `dev` and of the editor in `.moku/` stays), runs Bun again under `.moku/visual/bunfig.toml` as `dev` does (hot plugin, `--serve-plugin`, `--preload`), and the child serves the page on a free port, then stops it. No `manifest.json`: `[game] visual: no manifest.json in "<game>".` Exit 0 when the report is ok, else 1. `[game] visual: <file> must export default { app, tests }.` for a missing module or another shape, a bare app factory too.
- `preparePage(root, { agents?, preload?, servePlugins? })` of `@moku-labs/game/cli` writes the dev page of `moku-game dev` and resolves `{ html, bunfig, engine }` (both paths absolute; `engine` the `EngineFingerprint` whose `id` the page shows in `globalThis.__MOKU_GAME_ENGINE__`), for a server the caller starts: `bun --config=<bunfig>`. With agents the page also imports the game's `**/*.dev.ts` and hands them to the agents. It also writes the first, empty `.moku/assets-stamp.ts` when the game has none. The editor calls it: `await preparePage("games/timber", { agents: ["@moku-labs/editor/agent/page"] })`.
- `watchKeys(root, { onError? })` of `@moku-labs/game/cli` is the keys watch of `moku-game dev` for a server the caller runs: it runs the scan of `keys` once, resolves `{ close() }` after it, then scans again on a save of an asset or a strings file, and when a folder becomes or stops being a sub-feature. A failed scan calls `onError(message)` (default: a console warning `[game] keys: <message>`) and the watch goes on. The editor calls it next to `preparePage`: `const keys = await watchKeys("games/timber", { onError: message => log.warn(message) })`, then `keys.close()`. It rejects with the `[game]` errors of `preparePage` for a folder that is not a game.
- `watchEngine(root, { onChange?, onError? })` of `@moku-labs/game/cli` is the engine watch of `moku-game dev` for a server the caller runs: sync, it returns `{ close() }` and calls `onChange({ before, after, restart })` 300 ms after the installed engine changed, `restart: true` for a new version or dist (restart the page server), `restart: false` for a changed patch alone (run `bun install`); an engine from its sources is not watched. The editor calls it next to `preparePage`: `const engine = watchEngine("games/timber", { onChange: change => change.restart && restartPageServer() })`, then `engine.close()`.

## More patterns

```ts
import { exit, hint, play, schedule, slot, to, type } from "@moku-labs/game";
import { mergeFlight, mergeItems } from "./board";
import { defineFeature, defineFlow, defineNode } from "./state";

// Awaited effect with answers. The gate opens for these intents. The promise resolves with the answer.
export const confirmReset = defineNode({
  outcomes: { yes: type(), no: type() },
  over: true,
  run: async ({ fx, out }) => {
    const answer = (await fx({ kind: "popup", payload: { name: "reset" }, answers: ["yes", "no"] })) as {
      intent: string;
    };

    return answer.intent === "yes" ? out.yes() : out.no();
  }
});

// Timer: arm the clock, emit a cosmetic hint, then wait for `elapsed` at a rest node.
export const arm = defineNode({
  outcomes: { armed: type() },
  run: async ({ now, fx, out }) => {
    await fx(schedule(now + 60_000));
    fx.emit(hint("sparkle", { target: "dice" }));
    return out.armed();
  }
});

export const waiting = defineNode({
  outcomes: { elapsed: type<{ now: number }>(), skip: type() },
  rest: true,
  inbox: ["elapsed"]
});

// Sub-flow with a mapped edge and two exits.
const pick = defineNode({ outcomes: { picked: type<{ face: number }>(), back: type() }, rest: true });
const apply = defineNode({
  input: type<{ value: number }>(),
  outcomes: { done: type() },
  run: ({ input, player, out }) => {
    player.coins += input.value;
    return out.done();
  }
});

export const bonusFlow = defineFlow("bonus", {
  nodes: { pick, apply },
  start: "pick",
  outcomes: { finished: type(), left: type() },
  edges: {
    pick: { picked: to("apply", (payload: { face: number }) => ({ value: payload.face * 2 })), back: exit("left") },
    apply: { done: exit("finished") }
  }
});

// Main flow with the sub-flow as a node and a slot.
const lobby = defineNode({ outcomes: { bonus: type() }, rest: true, checkpoint: true });

export const main = defineFlow("main", {
  nodes: { lobby, bonus: bonusFlow, afterBonus: slot("afterBonus") },
  start: "lobby",
  edges: {
    lobby: { bonus: "bonus" },
    bonus: { finished: "afterBonus", left: "lobby" },
    afterBonus: { done: "lobby" }
  }
});

// A flight that does not close the gate: the flight starts, the merge commits on this edge, the next drop is
// taken in the next frame. The timeline keeps the view it started with, so the item flies on after the commit.
export const merge = defineNode({
  input: type<{ from: string; to: string }>(),
  outcomes: { done: type() },
  run: ({ input, player, fx, out }) => {
    fx.start(play(mergeFlight, { item: { projection: "board.items", key: input.from } }));
    mergeItems(player.board, input.from, input.to);
    return out.done();
  }
});

// Feature: contributes a sub-flow to the slot. A feature name must differ from every flow id.
const thanks = defineNode({ outcomes: { ok: type() }, rest: true, over: true });
const thanksFlow = defineFlow("thanksPopup", {
  nodes: { thanks },
  start: "thanks",
  outcomes: { done: type() },
  edges: { thanks: { ok: exit("done") } }
});

export const thanksFeature = defineFeature("thanks", {
  flows: [thanksFlow],
  contribute: { afterBonus: { flow: thanksFlow, order: 10 } }
});
```

### Tutorial guide

A tutorial step is data: the rest node derives it from the committed state with `guide`, so no save field and no `run` hold it.

```ts
export const awaitIntent = defineNode({
  rest: true,
  outcomes: { merge: type<{ from: string; to: string }>(), tutorialBlocked: type() },
  guide: ({ session }) =>
    session.tutorial === 2
      ? {
          allow: { intent: "merge", payload: { from: "c2", to: "c3" } },
          target: [{ projection: "board.items", key: "c2" }, { projection: "board.items", key: "c3" }],
          pad: 8,
          veil: false,                                  // the game draws its own look in an <anchor>
          blocked: { intent: "tutorialBlocked" }        // a press outside the window, or one inside the narrow refuses, answers this
        }
      : undefined
});
```

- `guide` runs when the node is entered (after its `onEnter` stages) and again after a commit while it waits at its gate (never for the commit of an edge); an equal result (deep JSON) changes nothing, a new one replaces the guide, `undefined` lifts it. It goes when the node is left; a restore enters the node again, so it is derived again. Fast mode: only the narrow. A `guide` that throws fails the node: `[game] The guide of node "path" threw: <message>` (rollback, retry, safe node). A dev build fails it when `blocked.intent` is no outcome of the node.
- The gate takes only `allow` and `blocked` while a guide stands; `app.flow.gate.state()` reports `blocked`. A press `input` gives that the open gate's narrow refuses (another intent, or `allow`'s intent with another payload, a drop on the wrong cell) answers `blocked` in its place, once, with its payload; without `blocked` it answers nothing. A press at a closed gate is held as it is, not converted.
- `ui` draws a veil (black 0.6, or `veil: { color, alpha }`; `alpha: 0` invisible, `false` none) around a window over the target or the union of the shown targets, grown by `pad`, placed every frame (it follows a moving or scrolling target), and locks `input` outside the window: a press there reaches no view (no `Tappable`, `LocalWrite`, scroll, drag, trace) and answers `blocked`, or nothing. No target, or none shown: the veil covers the screen and every press is locked, so a target key that never shows soft-locks the step (only `blocked` and the keyboard answer); a dev build warns `ui:guide-target-missing` `{ targets }` once after a key named no entity two frames in a row. A guide derived again with the same targets keeps the previous window for two frames while its targets are not laid out yet. A text field outside the window opens no keyboard. The doors `app.input.tap/press/drag` do no hit test and are not locked; a press reads the window of the frame before (input runs before layout). 0 B a frame.
- `await fx(guide({ allow: { intent: "roll" } }))` in a body still works, with the same options. The rounded window, the rim, the glide, the hand and the text are the game's: an `<anchor>` on the same targets with `veil: false`.

## Graph rules checked at `run()`

- Every outcome of every node has an edge. Every edge names a node of the same flow or a declared flow outcome.
- The start node is in `nodes`. Every node is reachable from the start node.
- A cycle needs at least one rest node.
- Every `inbox` type is an outcome of its node. A rest node has outcomes or a `run` body.
- Every edge of a `barrier` node leads to a rest node of the same flow.
- Flow ids are unique. A feature name is not a flow id. It is also not a plugin name: `time`, `lifecycle`, `model`, `clock`, `flow`, `world`, `renderer`, `input`, `assets`, `scenes`, `anim`, `i18n`, `text`, `ui`, `effects`, `audio`, `platform`, `log`, `env`.
- Two contributions of one slot need different `order` values.
- `safeNode` is the path of a checkpoint node.
- `recover` is allowed on a rest node only. On a node that is not `safeNode` it is a warning: it never runs there.
- A flow above 15 nodes is a warning. Split it into sub-flows of 7 to 15 nodes.

## Plugins

Registered in this order: `time`, `lifecycle`, `model`, `clock`, `flow`; then the list `screen` a game spreads in: `world`, `renderer`, `input`, `assets`, `scenes`, `anim`, `i18n`, `text`, `ui`; then the opt-in `effects`, `audio` and `platform` when the game adds them, `platform` last. `log` and `env` from `@moku-labs/common` are on every context as `ctx.log` and `ctx.env`. Configure with `createApp({ pluginConfigs: { <name>: { ... } } })`. Global config: `createApp({ config: { orientation, referenceSide } })`, defaults `"portrait"` and `1080`; a game passes them through `defineGameApp({ orientation, referenceSide, referenceLong })`.

### time (Standard, no dependencies, emits `time:thermal` and `time:rate`)

The single `requestAnimationFrame` loop. Six phases in this order: `input`, `animate`, `layout`, `sync`, `signals`, `render`.
- API: `onFrame(phase, callback): () => void`, `snapshot(): Readonly<Time>`, `setScale(scale)`, `pause()`, `resume()`, `isPaused()`, `isRunning()`, `step(deltaMs)`, `wake()`, and for an agent build (dev pages and `--debug` builds) `measure(listener): () => void` (every frame's `FrameMeasure`: gap, skipped ticks, the six phase durations, work, `rateMs`), `agentClock()` (the page clock, `undefined` without the flag) and `chargeAgent(ms)` (for engine plugins: the editor's own work left out of a frame). Every build: `rate(): Readonly<Time.FrameRate>` (`{ fps, mode, reason, displayHz, ladder, thermal }`, one frozen object until it changes), `setRate(choice: "auto" | 30 | 60 | 120)` (a number forces the cap, never above `maxFps`; `"auto"` gives it back; answers `rate()`), and for engine plugins `frameDrawn()` and `frameProbed()` (the renderer reports a drawn frame and a warm-up frame).
- Adaptive frame rate: `time: { maxFps: 120, adaptive: { floor: 60 } }` runs at the highest divisor of the display rate at or below `maxFps` (120 on a 120 Hz panel, 60 on a 60 Hz one, 72 on 144 Hz), drops one step when at least `max(8, 10 %)` of the last second's drawn intervals came late, returns one step after the dwell (5 s, doubling up to 120 s after a failed return) with 90 steady drawn frames in 3 s, never below `floor`; thermal `moderate` drops a step, `severe` to the floor. Only drawn frames count. Every change emits `time:rate` (`Time.RateChange`: `from`, `to`, `reason`, `mode`, `displayHz`, `thermal`, `window`, `dwellMs`) and logs `time: frame rate`. Off by default, in a headless app and on a fake clock. The render scale it may lower first is `pluginConfigs.renderer.adaptiveScale`, of type `AdaptiveScale` (`{ floor: 0.75, devices: "phone" }`).
- Native frame rate: on a page with `__MOKU_NATIVE__` of version 1, `time` asks the panel for the loop's rate at start and on every change, and hands it back at stop, every build; with `adaptive` the answer's `maxHz` is the display rate. In an agent build or with `adaptive` its one `moku-native:thermal` listener emits `time:thermal` with `Time.ThermalReading` (`{ status, headroom, at, android }`).
- `Time` is `{ delta, elapsed, scale, frame, idle }` in scaled milliseconds.
- Idle cap: after `idleAfterMs` unscaled milliseconds without a `wake()` the loop runs at `idleFps` and `snapshot().idle` is true. `wake()` lifts it at once; `input`, `anim`, `flow`, `assets`, `scenes`, `text` and `ui` call it. `step(deltaMs)` is never capped.
- Config: `maxFps: 30 | 60 | 120` default `60`, `maxDeltaMs: number` default `50`, `idleFps: 0 | 30` default `30` (`0` turns the idle cap off), `idleAfterMs: number` default `2000`, `adaptive: false | { floor: 30 | 60 }` default `false`.
- In plain Bun there is no frame source. `isRunning()` is false and tests drive frames with `step`.

### lifecycle (Standard, depends on time)

The stack of pause reasons. The game is paused while the stack is not empty.
- API: `push(reason)`, `pop(reason)`, `reasons(): readonly PauseReason[]`, `isPaused()`.
- Named reasons: `"background"`, `"devtools"`, `"system-dialog"`, `"device-lost"`. Any other string is allowed.
- Event `lifecycle:changed`: `{ reason, action: "push" | "pop", reasons, paused, resumed }`. `resumed` is true only on the change that emptied the stack.
- No config.

### model (Very Complex, no dependencies)

The `session` tree and the save document `{ player, rng }`. Modules `store` and `rng`.
- `store`: `load()`, `snapshot(): { player, session, rng }` frozen, `begin(): Transaction`, `markRest()`, `markBarrier(txId)`, `rollback()`, `restore({ player, session?, rng? })`, `flush()`.
- `rng`: `peek(id): number | undefined`.
- `load()` hands the whole document to `provider.commit()` at once when it rewrote the save: a new player and a migrated save are stored before the first node runs. A save at the current version produces no commit.
- A game reads `app.model.store.snapshot()`. The runner calls the rest. A node never calls the model.
- Event `model:committed`: `{ roots: readonly ("player" | "session" | "rng")[]; cause: "edge" | "rollback" | "restore" | "load" }`.
- Config: `playerProvider: PlayerStateProvider | undefined` default `undefined` which means in-memory, `initialPlayer: Json` default `{}`, `initialSession: Json` default `{}`, `seed: "from-save" | number` default `"from-save"`, `schemaVersion: number` default `1`, `migrations: readonly Migration[]` default `[]`.
- `PlayerStateProvider`: `load(): Promise<{ state: Json; version: number } | null>`, `commit(patches, version): void`, `commitDurable(patches, txId, version): Promise<void>`, `flush(): Promise<void>`.
- `Migration` is `{ from: number; up(state: Json): Json }`. `up` of `from: n` produces version `n + 1`. It works on the whole save document.
- `SaveUnreadableError` has `savedVersion` and `schemaVersion`. `flow.run()` rejects with it when the save is newer, a step is missing, a step throws or the shape is wrong.

### clock (Standard, no dependencies, no events)

Trusted time as an input. Monotonic `now()` and one `elapsed` signal at the next due moment.
- API: `now()`, `scheduleAt(moment | undefined)`, `onElapsed(listener): () => void`, `poke()`, `dueAt()`.
- Config: `source: ClockSource | undefined` default `undefined` which means the system clock. `ClockSource` is `{ now(), setTimer(callback, delayMs), clearTimer(handle) }`.
- A node never touches the clock. It awaits `fx(schedule(moment))`. `flow` posts `{ type: "elapsed", payload: { now } }` into its inbox when the moment arrives and when the game resumes.

### debug (Micro, no dependencies, no events)

The editor's overlay from the game, in every app. The plugin name `debug` is reserved.
- API: `app.debug.overlay.open({ mode?: "pill" | "card" })` (the card by default), `close()`, `toggle()` (hidden and the last visible mode), `isOpen()`. Each reads `globalThis.__MOKU_GAME_OVERLAY__` (set by the editor's page agent) at call time, else the 0.10 `editor.overlay`, and answers `true` when an overlay took the call; without the agent flag (a release build, a test) every member is a no-op answering `false`. A throwing channel logs `debug:overlay-failed`. The plugin instance is `debugPlugin`; it is always registered, a game never lists it.

### flow (Very Complex, depends on time, lifecycle, model, clock)

The graph. Modules `runner`, `gate`, `inbox`, `fx`, `features`. Runner methods sit on the plugin root.
- Runner: `run(): Promise<void>`, `onEnter(stage: "begin" | "load" | "scene", callback): () => void` (stages run in that order, each awaited; a `"begin"` callback must not wait: `scenes` shows the veil there before `assets` downloads at `"load"`), `walk(route, options?: { from?: Bookmark }): Promise<FlowState>`, `bookmark(): Bookmark`, `restore(bookmark): Promise<void>`, `describe(): FlowGraph`, `state(): FlowState`, `history(): readonly JournalEntry[]`, `setMode("live" | "fast")`.
- `gate.answer({ intent, payload? }): boolean` is the one entry of player answers. `gate.pointer(active)`. `gate.state(): { open, allowed, narrowed, blocked? }` (`blocked` while a guide names the answer of a press outside its window).
- `inbox.post({ type, payload? })` queues a world event. One entry per type. It is delivered only to a rest node whose `inbox` lists the type.
- `fx.handle(kind, handler, options?: { runInFast?: boolean }): () => void` registers the single handler of one effect kind. `fx.dispatch(descriptor)` is fire-and-forget. An awaited effect without a handler resolves `undefined` at once.
- `features.register(name, description)`, `features.all()`, `features.contributions(slotName)`.
- `FlowState` is `{ running, path, stack, pending: { fx?, gate? }, mode }`.
- `Bookmark` is `{ path, input, player, session, rng, graph, scene?, rest? }`. Serialisable. `scene` is written by the `game.bookmark` door and read by `game.restore`; `flow.restore` ignores it. `path` names a rest node, or the transit node that waits at the gate for an effect that takes answers (a `popup`, or a hand-written descriptor with `answers`); `rest: { path, input }` then names the rest point before it (left out when the graph started at that node or a restore entered it), and the state is the one committed when that node was entered. `restore` needs a running graph. A rest checkpoint is always accepted. Any other node is accepted only when the graph did not change since the bookmark; with another graph a transit bookmark is entered at `rest` instead when that is a checkpoint, and the log gets `flow:restore-fell-back`.
- After a rollback (a node failed) a view of a projection that the node moved and that still stands off its rest pose is settled, also when its item did not change. Ui elements are not settled by a rollback, and a timeline the failed node started without `await` runs on.
- A loop adds its sway on top of the value under it. The world compares that value with the rest pose, so a looping view that stands at home is never settled, and one a node moved is brought home while its loop runs on. A custom tween driver may report what its additive tracks add with the optional `offsetsOf(entity, component)`; without it the stored value is compared as it stands.
- The `loop` hook of a view runs while the world is live and `anim` is installed: a view that entered on a load, a mount or a restore gets its loop from the next live frame. `anim.finishAll()` ends it; the next flush of the world (a load, a restore, a commit in a paused or fast world) owes it again.
- For a JSX screen ui compares the description prop by prop, by value: inline styles are fine, an equal description costs nothing (no style pass, no layout, no write), hooks stay built once (a function compares by identity). A style object changed in place is not seen: build a new one. One node of a description, as the JSX runtime builds it, is a `DescriptionNode`.
- A projection may build a new item object on every commit. A view whose components did not change keeps its running motions; only a real component change cancels them. No frozen item tables are needed.
- After a `restore` or a load the picture is the one of the restored state, whatever played before: every view of a mounted projection stands on its rest pose, its `loop` starts again on the next live frame and no other motion runs, and every ui root is built again through the mount path, so `enter` hooks run and a loop starts as after a fresh mount. Scroll offsets, local state, hover and focus start anew. Look an element up again with `ui.find(key)` after a restore. A rest node names the scene it is shown on (`scene: "splash"`): a restore into a node without `scene` keeps the mounted scene.
- `restore` of a rest node resolves when the node is entered. `restore` of a transit node runs it again from its start, so its effects before the gate play again, and resolves once its gate is open. The open gate is not the draw: the popup shows on the next frame. `restore` also resolves when the loop ends before the bookmark was entered, after a stop or a fatal error, and nothing is entered then.
- Events: `flow:edge` `{ flow, node, outcome, payload, next, patches: { doc, session }, index, now }` after the commit of an edge. `flow:rest` `{ path, checkpoint }`. `flow:error` `{ path, error, rolledBackTo, retry }`.
- Config: `mainFlow` default `undefined` and required before `run()`, `safeNode: string | undefined` default `undefined` which means the main flow's `start`, `retries` default `1`, `settleTimeoutMs` default `2000`, `journalLimit` default `500`, `holdMs` default `0`.

### Screen plugins (V2, built)

`world`, `renderer`, `input`, `assets`, `scenes`. Each has a README at `src/plugins/<name>/README.md`; the root README lists their APIs, events and config. Rendering: WebGPU preferred, with Pixi's WebGL fallback.
- `app.scenes`: `current()` the mounted scene id, `expect(id)` the scene the next node without its own `scene` mounts, a rest node or a transit node in live mode (the restore door calls it; an unknown id throws). An `over` node takes it the same way, also over another mounted scene. A live switch, before it builds the scene, warms the bundles the scene names (`assets.warm`): their textures go to the GPU `renderer.uploads` a drawn frame while the old scene is still up, so the first frame of the new scene uploads none of them; textures already there are not waited for, and a fast walk or a headless app never waits. A bundle the scene does not name (a `core` bundle of portraits the board shows) is not warmed: name it in the scene's `bundles` or call `app.assets.warm`. Then, with a drawing renderer, the next scene is built aside: its ui elements are made by root and by part, laid out once and applied in parts, and the renderer makes its Pixi views, over the next frames off the stage in a budget per frame, config `scenes.buildMs: number | "auto"` (default `"auto"`, two thirds of the frame interval: 11.1 ms at 60 Hz, 5.56 ms at 120 Hz; `0` throws), and it is swapped in one frame. Until the swap `current()` answers the old scene, nothing of the new one is drawn, hit or found by `ui.find`, its `enter` motions wait and the gate stays closed, so the first tap lands on a complete scene; `scenes:changed` is emitted at the swap. A fast walk, a world that is not live and a headless app mount in one block as before. Over the scene being left, a live switch shows the look of `scenes.leave` (a veil, and a loader once the switch is not done `afterMs` after its start); the veil goes up at the node's `"begin"` stage, before `assets` downloads the coming scene at `"load"`, so a cold first visit reacts in the next frame.
- `Shape({ kind, w, h, fill, fillAlpha, alpha, radius, stroke, strokeWidth, dash, clip, sweep?, cap? })` (`kind: "rect"`; `sweep` and `cap` are optional, `1` and `"round"` when left out; only an arc reads them; a rectangle or a triangle ignores them, also when an earlier arc left them on the `Shape`): a rounded rectangle, `kind: "triangle"` (fills its box pointing right) or `kind: "arc"`: a stroke on the circle inscribed in the box (`min(w, h) − strokeWidth` across, centred) from 12 o'clock clockwise over `sweep` (0..1, clamped; 0 draws nothing, 1 a closed ring), ended by `cap` (`"round" | "butt"`); an arc draws no fill and ignores `radius` and `dash`. The path is built again only when a field changes: a still arc costs nothing a frame. `Shape({ kind: "arc", w: 28, h: 28, stroke: 0xc8a15a, strokeWidth: 2.2, sweep: 0.42 })` is a slot timer's ring with 42 % left.
- Overlays: `Overlay({ dim, dimColor, cover, hud, fade, hold })` on the root of an overlay (in `components`) keeps everything drawn before it as one picture, retaken in the frame anything in it changes, and with `cover: "opaque"` draws none of it once landed at alpha 1; `hold: true` (default `false`) holds the endless loops under it while it stands, as under a cover or a blurred picture (their phase follows time), so a dimmed sheet over a sharp scene draws no frame at rest; the engine draws the dim (`dim × level`, right under the root); the level follows the root's own enter and exit motion, `fade` (250 ms) only when it has none; level and landing are read through `app.renderer.sync.debug.overlays()`. A `backdrop: true` filter inside the kept range runs no pass while the picture stands (its look is in the picture) and is drawn again in the frame the overlay is gone. Types: `OverlayValue` (the component's value) and `HudPartValue` (a part of the HUD an overlay keeps shown or lets fade).
- HUD: a scene layer `{ above: "overlays" }` is the HUD layer, drawn above every overlay and never in a picture; a scene with a HUD layer and no `ui` gets `ui` right under it. Its roots never take the keyboard: Escape and the Back press reach the top sheet under it. `HudPart({ key })` tags a HUD view; an overlay's `hud` (`"all"`, `"none"` or keys) names the parts that stay shown, the others fade with its level and take no tap. Keys are typed by `defineGame<{ …, hud: "energy" | "gems" }>()`.
- Endless loops of views under an opaque or blurred overlay write nothing (`renderer.sync.loopsHeld(entity)`, the seam anim asks before an endless loop writes); their phase follows time.
- Scene switch look: from the start of a live switch (before its bundles and textures are awaited) the renderer draws a veil over the scene being left, above every layer, and, when the switch is not done `afterMs` after its start, a loader above it until the swap; then the veil fades out over the new scene. Config `scenes.leave` (default `{ cover: { color: 0x000000, alpha: 0.45, inMs: 50, outMs: 150 }, loader: { afterMs: 400 } }`) and a scene's `leave` (`defineScene("ward", { ..., leave: false })`) are merged field by field (the scene being left decides; `false` turns a part or the whole off); the loader is the engine's white ring, `loader: { texture: "ui.loader.ring" }` a game texture turning, or `loader: { projection: "loading" }` a projection in a layer of its own the scene declares (no other projection of the scene may draw there), kept built and hidden while the scene stands and shown once the loader is due; `scenes` feeds that loader the switch (`projection.feed`), so its `from(player, session, sw)` reads a `SceneSwitch`: `{ from: "ward", to: "ward", progress: 0 }` while the ward stands, then `{ from: "ward", to: "board", progress }`, the share of the board's bundles loaded (from `assets:bundle-progress`; a bundle loaded at the start or once the scene stage has its loads counts whole), 0 to 1 in steps of 0.01, the last exactly 1; `loader: { holdMs: 260 }` (default 0) is a floor on the swap: the next scene builds at once and the old one stays until 260 ms after the switch start and one drawn frame of the look, so a switch slower than it gets nothing added; an abort or a throw drops both at once; fast walks, a world that is not live, headless apps and the first scene show nothing and hold nothing. The scene being entered sets the veil's colour and alpha: `defineScene("night", { ..., enter: { cover: { color: 0x0b1020, alpha: 0.7 } } })` wins over what the scene being left resolved, field by field; `inMs`/`outMs` stay the left scene's and a veil turned off stays off. Types `SceneLeave`, `SceneCover`, `SceneLoader`, `SceneEnter` (`Scenes`).
- A scene names bundles on top of its `bundle` from the committed state: `defineScene("ward", { bundle: "episodes-kit", bundles: ({ session }) => [session.episode], layers: {}, projections: [wardRoom] })`. `bundles` is read each time a node enters the scene, and every way in (a live entry, a restore, the `safeNode` recovery) waits for all of them before the scene is mounted and the node's gate opens. The keys are `BundleKey`s of `generated/assets.ts`.
