- `app.assets`: `load(bundle)`, `warm(bundle)` (loads it if needed, then puts its textures and atlas pages on the GPU through `renderer.sync.textures.upload`, `renderer.uploads` a drawn frame; joins a running or finished warm; an unload forgets it; resolves also when the renderer could not upload; headless at once), `unload(bundle)`, `isLoaded(bundle)`, `has(bundle)` (the manifest carries it, loaded or not), `texture(key)`, `font(key)`, `audio(key)`, `usage()`. Per bundle in a feature's `assets.ts`: `defineBundles({ ep01: { tier: "feature", release: "leave", mipmaps: ["items/**"] } })`. `release: "leave"` also unloads the bundle, with reason `"leave"`, at the next rest once nothing holds it: not pinned by the node entered, not named by the mounted scene, no node of its feature on the stack; a bundle the outgoing scene named leaves one rest later. The default `"budget"` leaves only under the texture budget. `mipmaps` (`true` or globs relative to `assets/`) uploads the textures with their full chain; such a texture stays loose in a pack. A sub-feature with resources gets its own bundles, named like its folder, with `dir` and `parent` in the manifest; a code-only one has none. The effect `ready(bundle | bundles)` (root export, also from `defineGame`) lets a node rest on a load and stay answerable: its handler (fast mode too) answers `true` headless, throws for an unknown bundle, answers `true` when every bundle is loaded and warmed or its last warm failed (`ctx.log.warn("assets:ready-failed", { bundle, error })`, cleared by a later successful load), otherwise starts `warm` for what is missing, answers `false` and posts `{ type: "ready" }` into `flow.inbox` once all of it settled. Recipe: a rest node `inbox: ["elapsed", "ready"]` with outcomes `ready` and `back`, and a transit node `if ((await fx(ready(list))) === false) return out.wait();`. `companions.add({ load(bundle), unload(bundle) })` adds what loads and unloads with every bundle; `i18n` adds the strings of a sub-feature that way, only when `assets` is composed. Events `assets:bundle-loaded`, `assets:bundle-progress`, `assets:bundle-unloaded` (`reason: "budget" | "request" | "leave"`), `assets:replaced` (dev). Config: `manifest`, `textureBudgetMb: 192`, `preloadDepth: 2`, `baseUrl`, `io`.
- `resource(name, defaults)` clones plain JSON defaults into every world. `resource(name, () => value)` calls the factory once per world on first read, so the value may hold a `Map` or a function: `const Looks = resource("boardLooks", () => ({ shown: new Map<World.Entity, { look: string }>() }))`. A system keeps its own state there; `snapshot()` leaves a value that is not JSON out.
- `Now` is the engine resource of the frame's moment: `world` writes `clock.now()` into it at start and first thing in every frame, headless too, so every system of a frame reads one moment: `const { now } = res(Now)`; a fake clock makes it exact. A system that shows time writes its component only when its picture changes. `snapshot().resources` holds `Now: { now }`. Reserved resource names: `Now`, `Pointer`, `AnimPlayer`, `UiCounters`; a game resource of one of them throws `[game] world: the resource name "Now" is the engine's (the frame's moment).`
- When a system runs: before each run the world checks it. A system with a `query` is skipped while a term of its query has no entity (the smallest store among the terms is empty): no walk, no `mut()` mark, no timing. A system without a query always runs. `system({ ..., scenes: ["board"] })` runs only while one of those scenes is mounted or leaving: `scenes` calls `app.world.ecs.setScene(id)` at every switch, and the scene before leaves until nothing carries `Exiting` (the elements of its JSX views played their exit; the next scene's entities already stand then, so a `scenes` system writes only its own scene's entities). A dev build throws at start for a name in `scenes` no feature declares: `[game] System "board.idle" runs on the scene "bord", which no feature declares.` `ctx.resumed` is true on the first run after a skip (a cache or a remembered cue starts over then). The same for every system, the engine's included; 0 B a frame. A run with no rows does not happen any more: work a system did besides its rows (a hover, a drop or a press that ends, a resource reset, something that outlives its entities) goes to a system with `query: []` and `scenes`, reading its rows with `world.query()`. From 0.15.3: delete `systemsRun` from every feature (the type refuses it), rewrite the systems that work outside their rows, add `scenes` only to a system whose entities stand on every screen; `ecs.hold` and `ecs.isActive` are gone (a test asks `app.scenes.current()` or whether the system ran). World README, "When a system runs".
- Motion hooks are told why they play: `enter(view, item, hint, cause)` and `exit(view, item, hint, cause)` get `World.MotionCause`, `"mount"` (the view comes or goes with its screen: a mount, an unmount, a load, a restore, a paused or fast world) or `"change"` (a commit). A world projection plays them only for `"change"`; `ui` plays them for both. `app.world.projection.causeOf(entity)` answers how a view came or how it is leaving, also in a removal hook of its despawn, until the next frame.
- `app.world.projection.replace(spec)` swaps the spec of a registered projection; a mounted one runs its new `view` on the next frame. An unknown name throws. The caller is the dev hot swap.
- `projection({ …, initialOnly: [[Shape, ["sweep"]]] })`: `view` gives those fields once, at the birth of a view; after that they belong to another writer (a system drawing a timer arc from `Now`), and no changed item, motion, end-of-motion check (`world:view-corrected`), rollback, `settle`, restore or load writes or compares them, as with `mute()` for every view's whole life. Field names are checked per component; a pair with no field throws at register. Absent, every field is the projection's.
- `from(player, session, sw)`: the third argument is the switch another plugin last handed the projection with `projection.feed(name, sw)`, a `SceneSwitch` `{ from, to, progress }` (the scene left, the scene entered, `progress` 0 to 1), `undefined` for a projection never fed; a `from` with two parameters reads the state alone, as before. A loader reads it: `from: (_player, _session, sw: SceneSwitch | undefined) => ({ to: sw?.to ?? "", progress: sw?.progress ?? 0 })`. World README, "Feeding a projection".
- `app.input.lock.window(rect | null | undefined)`: the input lock `ui` sets for a guide (`Input.LockWindow` = `{ x, y, w, h }` in reference units, kept by reference and written in place); a press outside reaches no view and answers `flow.gate.state().blocked` or nothing, a drop or trace sample outside finds nothing; `null` locks everything, `undefined` lifts it. The doors `tap`, `press`, `drag`, `swipe`, `trace` are never locked.
- `input`: one followed pointer. A finger that has not started a gesture (pressed, inside the tap slop, no long press, no trace) gives way to the next finger that goes down, wherever it rests, and its press is cancelled; a finger that started a gesture keeps it. `Pointer.id` is the followed `pointerId` (`-1` at rest): a system that measures the finger's travel starts over when it changes.
- `Draggable({ payload, carry?, aim? })`: `aim: { x, y }`, a point of the view in its own units, moves the hover and the drop lookup from the finger to that point of the view in the hand; `null` (default) is the finger.
- `pluginConfigs.renderer.onDemand: true` draws a frame only when something visible changed (a written view, a filter value, a resize, a wake, a capture); `app.renderer.stats().drawn` is the frames drawn per second (`fps` without it); a game that writes into its own `Display` object calls `app.renderer.invalidate(entity)` before the write; `renderer.sync.debug.verifyFrames(true)` (dev/debug) checks skipped frames by pixels and logs `renderer:missed-frame`; a dev build warns `renderer:missed-mark` for a write without the call.
- `app.renderer.stats()` adds `textureMbSplit: { art, targets, kept }` (MiB). `app.renderer.host.resolution()` is the resolution drawn at: `override ?? min(devicePixelRatio, maxResolution)`; `maxResolution` is a number (default 2), a change of `devicePixelRatio` is followed from the next frame, and `app.renderer.monitor.setResolution(n | undefined)` overrides it in every build, the way to apply a player's graphics setting from an effect (0.5 to 4, else a `RangeError`).
- `app.renderer.monitor` (agent builds; nothing otherwise): `stream(listener)` the performance log, one frozen JSON line at a time (`PerfLogLine`, `v` = `PERF_LOG_VERSION` = 1, `t` page epoch ms, `build`): `header`, `startup`, a `sample` a second, `spike` (a frame over its budget, with its passes, GPU time, systems, compiles, filters per kind, long frames), `longFrame`, `event`, `mark`, `thermal`; `frames()` the frame ring (typed-array columns, `read(into, cursor)` copies without allocating; `frameAt(ring, age)` gives one record); `mark(label)`; `event(name, detail?)`; `beginAgent()`/`endAgent()` for engine plugins. Config `renderer.monitor: { budgetMs: "rate", frames: 1024 }`: `"rate"` makes the spike budget one frame of the frame's rate (8.33 ms at 120 fps, 16.7 at 60). The engine sends nothing anywhere. The types of the log and of its ring are exported from the root for tools that read it: `PerfLogLine` and its lines `PerfHeaderLine`, `PerfStartupLine`, `PerfSampleLine`, `PerfSpikeLine`, `PerfLongFrameLine`, `PerfEventLine`, `PerfMarkLine`, `PerfThermalLine`, `PerfCollectorLine`, with `PerfEventName`, `PerfChange`, `PerfChangeEntry`, `PerfCause`, `PerfDisplay`, `PerfMeasured`, `LongFrameEntry`, `PassKind`, `PassRecord`, `ProblemRule`, `ShaderWhat`, `OverlayWhat`, `OverlayEventDetail`, `PoolTrimDetail`, `WarmDetail`; the ring `FrameRing`, `FrameRecord`, `FrameColumns`, `FrameReadout`, `FrameReadResult`; the sections `MonitorSections`, `MonitorCounts`, `MonitorConfig`; and the constant lists `PERF_CAUSES` (bit order of the `causes` column), `PERF_GAP_BUCKETS`, `MONITOR_SECTIONS` and `DEMAND_REASONS` (the `reason` column's index into it).
- The telemetry of a debug build (0.15, PerfLog still `v: 1`, every field additive): the header carries `app: { id }` (`__MOKU_GAME_APP__`, `"com.mokulabs.timber.debug"` in a native debug build, else `null`) and `debug: { overdraw }`. The pass ring (`frames().passes`) gains `owner` (the entity whose filter drew the pass, 0 none), `kind2` (the filter kind, 1-based: `frames().kindNames[kind2 - 1]`, 0 none), `drawsAt` (the frame's draws when the pass began; WebGPU), `format` and `resolution` of its target; `frames().systemNames` names `sysIdx` (a new array when a system registers). A spike's `passes[]` add `owner`, `view` (the owner's view label), `filter`, `draws`, `format`, `resolution`, `kept`. Root exports `PASS_KINDS` (`passes.kind` by index), `SHADER_WHATS`, `PROBLEM_RULES`, types `ShaderEventDetail`, `ProblemEventDetail`, `PerfCounts`. Event `shader` `{ what: "compile" | "module", label, ms, frame, boot, during: { pass, filter, owner, view } }`, one per pipeline or shader module, written at the flush, boot compiles included (`boot: true`); the old `compile { frame, count }` stays. Event `problem` once per crossing, judged once a second: `filter-still` (a filtered view the kept cache does not keep stood still `stillFrames` drawn frames, filtered in every one over `stillMpx`; `reason: "budget" | "not-eligible"`), `target-churn` (render targets made and dropped `churnPerSecond` a second for `churnSeconds`, or made while idle, or within `churnAfterTrimMs` after a pool trim; `reason: "rate" | "idle" | "after-trim"`), `retakes` (a kept view taken again 3 times in 2 s; `value` per second); `{ rule, cleared: true, owner, view }` when it stops. Thresholds are flat keys of `renderer.monitor`: `stillFrames: 60, stillMpx: 0.25, churnPerSecond: 4, churnSeconds: 3, churnAfterTrimMs: 1000`. A `sample` adds `counts: { entities, views, timers, frameListeners, clockListeners, …registered }` (`timers` = `clock.pending()`; input registers `inputListeners`) and `targets: { created, destroyed }` (WebGPU, else `null`); `stats().counts` reads the same. `monitor.counts.register(name, read)` adds a count (agent builds; at most 16, the 17th throws `[game] Monitor count table is full (16).`; the renderer's `onStop` drops them). Event `debug { overdraw }` marks the overdraw switch. The editor's collector writes `telemetry` and `gap` lines into its copy of a log (`PerfTelemetryLine`, `PerfGapLine`); the engine never does.
- Overdraw heat map (dev and debug builds): `app.renderer.sync.debug.overdraw(true)` (or `game.debug { overdraw: true }`) draws every frame so a pixel's brightness counts the layers drawn there: 1/16 white a layer, white at sixteen. While on, every frame is drawn (also with `onDemand`), kept pictures draw live and filters are off; only the stage pass changes, the tree between frames stays the game's, and off draws the game again from the next frame. Texels a texture leaves transparent count nothing.
- `app.renderer.viewport.size()` answers one frozen object, replaced only when the frame changes (a resize, a rotation, new insets, a new scale): compare frames with `===`; a write into it throws a `TypeError`.
- `pluginConfigs.renderer.warm` (default `1`, 0 to 16) is the pipeline warm-up: while a game loads, each drawn frame first draws that many invisible probes (sprites, graphics, text, particles, every filter kind and stage `effects` registers, on the canvas and on a texture, with and without a clip), wiped by the stage pass, so no screen creates a GPU pipeline in the frame it opens in; `0` turns it off. `app.renderer.sync.filters.warm(filter)` warms a game's own filter (answers `true` once drawn). An agent build writes a `warm` event `{ draws }` when the queue empties.
- `defineFilter(id, { area: value => [x, y, width, height] })` declares the box, in the entity's own units, outside of which the filter draws nothing: Pixi renders and fills only that box (a lens over a full-screen cover fills its disc, not the screen). The view gets the union of its enabled filters' areas, none when an enabled filter declares none (`renderer.sync.filters.area(entity, area)`). The area also clips the view's own children: Pixi draws nothing of the view outside it, so a shadow or a badge that overhangs the box is cut; make the box hold them. The full-screen filter budget and the kept-picture budget count a view with an area by that area, not by its box. Distance-field text uses device pixels for its edge: sharper at a resolution above 1. The type of that box is `FilterArea`.
- `pluginConfigs.renderer.poolTrim` (default `{ restMs: 1000, aboveMb: 16 }`) gives back the idle render targets Pixi's texture pool keeps, strictly between frames: after `restMs` of a still screen (`onDemand`), `restMs` after a scene change (each when the targets grew by `aboveMb` MiB), and on a pause (whatever grew); `false` keeps them. `stats().textureMbSplit.targets` shows the drop; an agent build writes a `pool-trim` event `{ reason, freedMb }`. Its type is `PoolTrim`.
- `blend` on `Sprite` and `NineSlice` (optional, absent by default, type `SpriteBlend`): `"screen"` lightens what is under the view (CSS `mix-blend-mode: screen` on a dark background), `"add"` adds its colours (brighter), `"normal"` covers by alpha as without the field. Any other string draws normally and warns `renderer:blend-unknown` once. It goes on the view itself, so a glow's children draw normally; both are Pixi's native batch blends, no filter and no pass, and each switch between blends in draw order costs one draw call. In `ui`, `style.blend` on an `image`, an `icon` or a nine-slice style writes it (`style={{ blend: "screen" }}` for a soft glow, `"add"` for a spark); an element that never blended carries no `blend` field, so describe and saves stay as they were.
- `app.renderer.viewport.size().safeArea` is read from four CSS custom properties on the page, `--moku-safe-top`, `--moku-safe-right`, `--moku-safe-bottom`, `--moku-safe-left`, each falling back to `env(safe-area-inset-*, 0px)`. Any CSS length works (`max()`, `calc()`, `env()`); a negative one counts as 0. A change of a property or of the page's insets, and the window event `moku-native:insets`, is laid out at the next frame. There is no `setInsets`: set the properties, e.g. `:root { --moku-safe-top: max(env(safe-area-inset-top, 0px), 24px); }`.

### Interface plugins (V3, built)

A screen is a projection whose `view` returns JSX. The game's `tsconfig.json` sets `"jsx": "react-jsx"` and `"jsxImportSource": "@moku-labs/game"`; screens are `.tsx` files. There is no DOM and no React.

- Tags: `screen`, `layer`, `row`, `column`, `stack`, `spacer`, `panel` (swallows taps), `image` (`texture`, `fit?: "contain" | "cover" | "fill"`), `icon` (`name`, `fit?`), `text` (`content: string | Message`, or `bind={bind(Counter, "value")}` with `components={[Counter({ value })]}`; formats `int`, `mm:ss`, `h:mm:ss`, `duration`; `Countdown({ until })` with `bind(Countdown, "left", { format: "mm:ss" })` counts down to a `clock` moment; `style` is a text style key), `button` (`intent` + `payload`, or `local`, never both), `scroll` (`axis?: "x" | "y"` (`"y"`), fixed at spawn, another one later warns `ui:scroll-axis-fixed`; children for a short list, laid out as a column on `y` and a row on `x`, or the windowed form `rows`, `rowHeight`, `overscan?` (5), `row: index => node`, on `y` only: `axis: "x"` with `rows` throws `[game] A windowed scroll moves on y only.`; row state belongs in the model, a row that leaves the window loses its local state; `snap?: number[]` stops in offsets, kept inside `0..max`: a release glides to the stop nearest `offset + v × 260` (v in units a ms) on `1 − (1 − p)³` over `min(620, 260 + distance × 1.1)` ms; without `snap` a release flings, `v ×= 0.998` a ms until under 0.02, 0 when the finger rested over 50 ms; `offset?: number` (0) where it stands from the start, drawn there in its first frame, a new value glides there, the same value does nothing; hard edges, nothing passes on to a parent scroll; a press on a child that leaves the tap slop along the scroll's axis goes to the scroll and the child answers nothing, a finger on a moving scroll only stops it; every number in `time.delta` ms, so a time scale applies; the public component `ScrollState { offset, max, moving }` on its entity, whole units `0..max`, written when it changes and once with `moving: false` when it stops, read by a system and by `game.explain`; `app.ui.scroll(key, to)` and the visual step `{ scroll: { key, to } }` set it at once), `input` (a text field; its text lives in the component's `local`, see the ui README), `anchor` (`to: AnchorTarget | AnchorTarget[]`, `AnchorTarget` = `{ projection, key }`, a ui element keyed under its root's projection; `pad?: number` (0) outward in its root's units: its rect is where its targets are drawn, the union of the shown ones, in the frame they are laid out, scrolled or moved, through fits, slots and ancestor motion, rotation left out; children lay out inside it; a `width`/`height`/`position` in its style is ignored (`ui:anchor-style`, dev); with no target shown it is drawn at alpha 0 and takes no tap, stays, and comes back with its target; `ui:anchor-target-missing` `{ key, to }` once (dev) after a key named nothing two frames in a row; a target inside the anchor is refused, `[game] An anchor cannot point at its own child "key".`; its `change.Box` motion plays only when its targets change (a new `to`, a key naming another entity), never on a follow, and a glide that runs is carried so it lands on the moving target; 0 B a frame still or following: `<anchor key="window" to={{ projection: "board.strip", key: "seat0" }} pad={4} motion={glide}>`). Common props: `key`, `style`, `state: { active?, disabled?, selected? }`, `motion`, `components` (extra component values for the element's entity, such as a filter: `components={[Glow({ strength: 2 })]}`, or `DebugTrigger()`: five taps within 3000 ms of wall time on that view call `app.debug.overlay.open()` on a page with the agent flag, nothing elsewhere; put it on a `button` naming nothing); containers take `hosts?: string[]` (projections drawn inside the element: world views hang under it from the slot's first frame; a JSX projection is laid out in the slot's content box). Children draw and are hit in markup order at equal `zIndex`; the roots of a scene draw in the order of its `projections` (the `ui` layer sorts by `Order`; `ui: { sort: "none" }` keeps insertion order). `defineMotion({ when: "change" })` plays its `enter` and `exit` only for a commit or a popup, never when its screen mounts or unmounts; declare a motion at module level (`ui:motion-rebuilt` names a loop rebuilt in a view). `motion.change` plays `Box` (the rects), `Transform` (the rest poses), the visual the element is drawn with (`Shape`, `Sprite`, `NineSlice`, `Text`, when a render or a restyle moves a number of it: `sweep`, `alpha`, `w`; a returned motion brings the numbers home from where they stand and the other fields land at once; the last motion of that name is cancelled first) and each extra of `components`, each as `(view, previous, next, hint)`; a dev build names any other `change` hook once, `ui:change-never-plays` `{ key, name }`. An element a render replaces (a root whose view returns another key or tag, a child of another key or tag) plays its exit with `"change"`, everything under it plays its own, and it leaves `find` at once, so the new element takes the keys they share. Style adds `nineSlice`, `tint`, `offsetX`, `offsetY`, `scale`, `origin`, `fit: "contain"`; state variants `is: { hover, pressed, disabled, active, selected, covered }`. `popup(Component, props, { over })` stacks a popup over a kept one.
- Style vocabulary (`defineStyle`, plain data): flow `direction`, `wrap`, `justify`, `align`, `alignSelf`, `gap`, `grow`, `shrink`; box `padding`, `margin`, `width`, `height`, `minWidth`, `minHeight`, `maxWidth`, `maxHeight`, `aspect`, `overflow`; position `position`, `left`, `top`, `right`, `bottom`, `reason`; visual `fill`, `stroke`, `strokeWidth`, `radius`, `alpha`, `shape: "rect" | "triangle" | "arc"` (`"rect"`; a triangle fills the box pointing right; an arc is only a `stroke` of `strokeWidth` on the circle inscribed in the box, `min(width, height) − strokeWidth` across, from 12 o'clock clockwise over `sweep`), `dash` (dash length of the stroke, gaps of half a dash; not on an arc), `sweep` (0..1, default 1, clamped; 0 draws nothing, 1 a closed ring), `cap: "round" | "butt"` (`"round"`; the ends of an open arc); variants `is: { pressed?, disabled?, active?, selected? }` and `when: { portrait?, landscape?, tall?, wide? }`, each a partial style merged in when the flag holds. Lengths are reference units or `"safeArea.top" | "safeArea.right" | "safeArea.bottom" | "safeArea.left"`. No font size here: it comes from the text style.
- `defineComponent(name, { local?, outcomes?, view(props, local) })`. A component with `outcomes` is a popup: `await fx(popup(Component, props))` opens the gate for its outcomes and resolves with `{ intent, payload }` of the pressed button. A button with `local` writes into the nearest component instance; it never reaches the graph.
- `tr(key, params?)` returns a frozen `Message` `{ key, params }`; no locale is read at the call site. Strings live in `strings/<locale>.json` of any feature or sub-feature, as ICU MessageFormat 1 (`{n, plural, one {# order} other {# orders}}`, `select`, `selectordinal`, `number`, `date`, `time`; no skeletons, no `currency`). `bun run assets:keys` compiles them. The keys of the top-level features and the layers go into `generated/strings.<locale>.ts`, which one feature registers; a sub-feature's keys start with `<name>.` (`ep01.title`) and go into `generated/strings.<name>.<locale>.ts`, which the sub-feature registers lazily, `strings: { en: () => import("@generated/strings.ep01.en"), ru: () => import("@generated/strings.ep01.ru") }`. With `assets` composed those modules load and unload with the bundle named like the sub-feature: every way the bundle comes (a node entry, a scene's `bundles`, `load`, a restore, the `safeNode`) brings its strings, a locale switch brings them in the new locale, and while the bundle is not loaded a key of it gives `⟦key⟧` and `has(key)` is false. A compiled module calls the root helpers `messageArgument(value, intl)` (an element stays an element part, a list goes through `Intl.ListFormat`, a number through `Intl.NumberFormat`, else text) and `messageDuration(ms)` (`95_000` gives `{ minutes: 1, seconds: 35 }`). `app.i18n`: `locale()`, `setLocale(locale)` (async, emits `i18n:locale-changed`), `format(message, locale?)` returns `Part[]`, `plain(message)` returns a string, `has(key)`, `isKey(value)`, `locales()`, `replace(locale, messages)` (dev hot swap of a generated strings file). Config: `locale: "en"`, `fallback: "en"`, `locales: {}`.
- Keys that come from data: `I18n.TextKey<Strings>` is the keys of the generated `Strings` without parameters (nothing new is generated). A data table types its keys `TextKey` or builds them with the kit's `key("board.hint.red")`; the kit's `tr` never takes a plain `string`. A key read back from a save is checked where the app is (an effect handler, app or page code, loading a save) with one `isKey(value)`: `defineGameApp({ ..., strings: type<Strings>() })` types the game's `app.i18n`, so a true `app.i18n.isKey(value)` narrows the value to `TextKey`; `ctx.require(i18nPlugin).isKey(value)` in a plugin narrows to `string`. `app.i18n.isKey(value)` answers true for a key of the loaded tables of the current locale or the fallback, and for the `<feature>.` prefix of a sub-feature whose strings are not loaded yet; a key that takes parameters answers true too.
- Text: `Text` component, `label({ text, style, at, anchor? })` for board text in a projection view, `defineTextStyles({ "hud.digits": { font, size, fill, bold?, italic?, stroke?, strokeWidth?, letterSpacing?, align?, wrap? (a width, "none" or "box": wrap at the laid-out width of its ui element), digits?, lineHeight? (the line as a multiple of size above 0, such as 1.28; glyphs sit in the middle of the line; absent: the font's own line) } })` under the feature's `textStyles` key. Tags inside a string: `<b>`, `<i>`, `<color=#rrggbb>`, `<icon=key>`, `\<`, `\n`. Built-in styles `body` and `digits` from config `fonts: { body: "ui.font-body", digits: "ui.font-digits" }`. `app.text.measure(content, style, width?)` gives the same numbers in a browser and in Bun. `app.text.replaceStyles(styles)` is the dev hot swap of a saved `defineTextStyles` value.
- Animation is data: `defineAnimation(id, { slots: { name: type<Anim.Target>() }, build: (slots, { at }) => Step })`. Steps: `sequence(...)`, `parallel(...)`, `stagger(items, ms, item => Step)`, `tween(target, Component, to, { ms, ease?, delayMs?, additive?, space?, reduced? })`, `set(target, Component, patch)`, `wait(ms)`, `mark(name)`, `frames(target, { keys, fps, loop? })`, `sfx(key, { bus? })`, `haptic(kind)`, `use(animation, slots, tools?)`, `spawn` (a temporary entity, flying coins, that the timeline despawns when it ends; see the anim README). `Frames({ keys, fps, loop, playing })` is a component that walks a sprite through its textures for the entity's whole life. A target is `{ projection, key }` or an entity. A timeline resolves each `{ projection, key }` target once, when it starts: every step writes the view that held the key then, also after a commit removed it and while its exit plays, until it despawns; a view spawned again under the same key is not followed, and a key nothing held at the start is looked up at its step. `reduced: "keep"` (on a `tween` step, `transition` and `loop` of `defineMotion`, `TweenOptions`, `RestOptions`) plays a track as written under reduced motion, a fade for one; the default `"cut"` lands it at once or holds a loop on its first key. A node plays it with `await fx(play(animation, slots))`; in fast mode it finishes at once. `defineMotion({ states, transition?, on: { enter?, exit?, change? }, when? })` builds the enter, exit and change hooks for a projection or the `motion` prop of a tag; `when: "change"` plays enter and exit only for a commit, so an element that comes or goes with its screen stands at rest and leaves without a motion (default `"always"`). Events `anim:mark` `{ animation, mark }` and `anim:finished` `{ animation }`. `app.anim.replace(definition)` is the dev hot swap: the next `play` builds the new tree. A system cannot `require` a plugin, so it plays through the resource `AnimPlayer`: `res(AnimPlayer).play(animation, slots)` returns the same handle as `app.anim.play`, and the registered animation of `animation.id` wins, so a hot swap reaches the system. Play on a change, never every frame; from phase `input` the tree moves in `animate` of the same frame. Before `anim` starts it throws `[game] AnimPlayer is not ready: anim has not started.` Config `maxTracks: 2000`.
- A `tween` step takes `segments` and `repeat` as `ViewHandle.tween` does: `tween(chest, Transform, { y: 0, scale: 0 }, { ms: 2400, additive: true, repeat: "forever", segments: [{ at: 0.08, ease: "out", to: { y: -14, scale: 0.06 } }, { at: 1, to: { y: 0, scale: 0 } }] })`. Segments walk over `ms` on one clock, `to` is where the last one ends, an additive walk names offsets; a number counts the extra runs. A definition error throws for empty segments, an `at` outside 0..1 or out of order, a last segment before 1, a bad repeat, and a `sequence` step after one that never ends. A forever step ends only by cancel or finish (a finish and a fast world land it on its start pose), does not play under reduced motion `"cut"`, writes nothing while its view is unseen, and lets the clock idle; a system plays it once through `AnimPlayer` and keeps the handle.
- Audio is opt-in: `plugins: [...screen, audioPlugin]`. `fx(sfx("orders.complete"))` resolves when the sound started. `await fx(music("board.theme"))` cross-fades; `music(null)` fades out; a scene's `music` key switches the track on `scenes:changed`. Buses `master`, `music`, `sfx`. Volumes come from the committed player: config `volumes: player => (player as Player).settings.audio`, applied on every `model:committed`. `app.audio`: `setVolume(bus, value)`, `volume(bus)`, `mute(bus, on)`, `muted(bus)`, `unlocked()`, `journal()` (the last started sounds, empty unless config `journal` is above 0). Config: `buses: { master: 1, music: 0.6, sfx: 1 }`, `musicFadeMs: 600`, `volumes`, `context`, `journal: 0`, `music: "decode" | "stream"` default `"decode"` (gapless buffer; `"stream"` is an `<audio>` element, less memory, a gap at every loop), `session: "ambient" | "playback" | "auto"` default `"ambient"` (iOS only: ambient mixes with other apps and obeys the silent switch). The context is asked to run at start: where the shell lets audio play (a native webview with the gesture requirement off) `unlocked()` is true with no touch; a browser that wants a gesture unlocks on the first `pointerdown` or `touchend`. Without `audio` every `sfx` and `music` effect resolves `undefined` at once, so the same node runs in a game with no sound. Named sounds: `sfx(key, { bus?, id?, fadeMs? })` with an `id` plays through its own gain, and the next sound with the same `id` fades the old one out over `fadeMs`, else config `sfxFadeMs` (default `120`, real milliseconds); `fx.start(stopSfx(id, { fadeMs? }))` and `app.audio.stop(id, { fadeMs? })` fade it out and end it (`fadeMs: 0` cuts it); an `id` nothing plays under changes nothing, and a sound of that `id` still decoding never starts. Without `id` an `sfx` plays to its end as before.
- `app.ui`: `tree()` the live screen as plain data (a text node carries `content`, the words it draws after `tr()` and `bind`; a text field carries `value`), `find(key)` the entity of a keyed element, `fill(key, value)` types into the text field with that `key`, `scroll(key, to)` puts the `scroll` with that `key` at `to` from its start at once, inside `0..max`, its fling or glide stopped (`false` and `ui:scroll-without-scroll` for no live `scroll`, `false` and `ui:scroll-before-solve` for a `scroll` its first solve has not placed yet), `rectOf(target)` where an `AnchorTarget` (or the shown ones of a list) is drawn, in screen reference units, the rect an `<anchor>` sits on, a target of no area shown at its point (`{ x, y, w: 0, h: 0 }`; an `<anchor>` on it stands there at size 0, takes no tap, its children lay out and hit as usual; an inward `pad` past half the target leaves it at size 0 on the centre), `undefined` when none is shown (an `image` whose style states a size, `width`/`height` or both edges of an absolute one, laid out at 0 draws nothing and counts as not shown; one whose style states no size keeps its alpha and draws as its `Sprite` says, ui never writing the size a game's system gives it), any build, a new object per call (`app.ui.rectOf({ projection: "board.strip", key: "seat0" })` → `{ x: 40, y: 1500, w: 116, h: 120 }`), `lint()` tap targets under `tapTargetPt` (default `44`), text that overflows in some locale, absolute elements without `reason`. Config: `tapTargetPt: 44`, `breakpoints: { tall: 2, wide: 1.5 }`. `ui` emits only the dev global event `ui:hot-swap`, see "Hot swap".

```tsx
// features/hud/view.tsx
import type { Anim } from "@moku-labs/game";
import { Transform, mark, sequence, sfx, tween, type } from "@moku-labs/game";
import { defineAnimation, defineComponent, defineFeature, defineTextStyles, projection, tr } from "../../state";

export const hud = projection({
  name: "hud",
  layer: "ui",
  from: player => ({ coins: player.coins }),
  view: hud => (
    <row key="bar" style={{ gap: 16, padding: { top: "safeArea.top", left: 24, right: 24 }, width: "100%", height: 120 }}>
      <text key="coins" style="hud.digits" content={tr("hud.coins", { n: hud.coins })} />
      <button key="settings" intent="openSettings" style={{ width: 96, height: 96 }}><icon name="hud.gear" /></button>
    </row>
  )
});

export const RewardPopup = defineComponent("RewardPopup", {
  outcomes: { claim: type<{ orderId: string }>() },
  view: (props: { orderId: string; gold: number }) => (
    <panel key="reward" style={{ nineSlice: "ui.panel", direction: "column", gap: 16, padding: 32, width: 600, height: 400, fit: "contain" }}>
      <text key="gold" style="hud.digits" content={String(props.gold)} />
      <button key="claim" intent="claim" payload={{ orderId: props.orderId }} style={{ width: 240, height: 88 }}>
        <text content={tr("common.claim")} />
      </button>
    </panel>
  )
});

export const popCoins = defineAnimation("hud.popCoins", {
  slots: { coins: type<Anim.Target>() },
  build: ({ coins }) => sequence(tween(coins, Transform, { scale: 1.2 }, { ms: 120 }), tween(coins, Transform, { scale: 1 }, { ms: 200 }), sfx("hud.coins"), mark("done"))
});

export const hudFeature = defineFeature("hud", {
  projections: [hud],
  ui: [RewardPopup],
  animations: [popCoins],
  textStyles: defineTextStyles({ "hud.digits": { font: "ui.font-digits", size: 40, fill: 0xffe082, digits: true } }),
  strings: { en: () => import("../../generated/strings.en") }
});

// features/orders/deliver.ts — the popup and the choreography are effects the node awaits
import { play, type } from "@moku-labs/game";
import { defineNode, popup } from "../../state";
import { popCoins, RewardPopup } from "../hud/view";

export const deliver = defineNode({
  outcomes: { claimed: type<{ orderId: string }>() },
  run: async ({ player, fx, out }) => {
    const answer = (await fx(popup(RewardPopup, { orderId: "o1", gold: 5 }))) as { intent: "claim"; payload: { orderId: string } };

    player.coins += 5;
    await fx(play(popCoins, { coins: { projection: "hud", key: "coins" } }));
    return out.claimed({ orderId: answer.payload.orderId });
  }
});
```

### effects (V5, Complex, opt-in)

Cosmetic rendering extras as data, drawn by `effectsPlugin`: `plugins: [...screen, effectsPlugin]`. Nothing here enters `model`, the journal or a save. Headless it draws nothing. The full reference is `src/plugins/effects/README.md`.
- Particles: `defineEmitter(id, config)` returns frozen data a feature lists under `emitters`. Required: `textures` (1 to 16 asset keys of one atlas page) and exactly one of `burst` (an integer, emitted once) and `rate` (particles per second while `active`). Optional with defaults: `lifeMs`, `speed`, `angle`, `gravity`, `drag`, `spin`, `shape` (`point`, `circle`, `rect`, `ring`), `scale`, `alpha`, `tint` (each `{ from, to }`), `space` (`"world"` or `"local"`), `prewarmMs`, `maxParticles` (`256`), `blend` (`"normal"` or `"add"`). A mistake throws at definition.
- The `Emitter({ effect, active })` component on an entity runs an emitter: `generator: item => [Sprite({ texture: "board.generator" }), Emitter({ effect: "fx.steam" })]`. `effect: ""` draws nothing. Particles step in the `animate` phase, so they freeze while paused and a fast walk emits nothing. Their random source is seeded, never `Math.random` and never the model's rng. In `defineGame<Types>()`'s `Emitter`, `effect` takes the game's emitter ids and `""`; `defineEmitter` never takes `""`.
- Filters: `defineFilter(id, { wgsl, glsl, uniforms?, passes?, padding?, inputs?, fallback? })` returns a component type a feature lists under `filters`. Both bodies are required: `wgsl` is the WGSL `fn mainFragment` and reads a uniform as `fu.amount`; `glsl` is GLSL ES 3.0 `void main()` that sets `finalColor` and reads a uniform as `amount`. A uniform is a number (tweenable), `{ color: 0xffd700 }` or an array of 2 to 4 numbers. Every filter component also has `enabled: true` and `order: 0`. A filter covers the entity's subtree; on a ui element it goes in the `components` prop.
- Kept pictures: a still filtered view is drawn as one quad from an engine-owned picture, also while it moves (`renderer.keptMb`, default 64; `0` turns it off; `renderer.sync.debug.kept(false)` draws everything live). `defineFilter(id, { cache?: "local" | "placed" | false })`, default `"local"`; a body that reads `uOutputFrame.xy`, `uGlobalFrame`, `gl_FragCoord`, `@builtin(position)` or `uOutputTexture` and declares nothing is drawn live (dev warns `effects:filter-reads-screen`); write `canvasPixel(uv)` for the pixel's canvas position (in WGSL and GLSL) and it is kept; `cache: false` draws it live always. `app.renderer.stats()` measures `renderPasses` on the GPU path in every build and adds `renderPassesMax` (the most of one frame in the last second), `canvasPasses` and `canvasPassesMax` (the same for the passes on the canvas: breaks = `canvasPasses - 1`; where nothing counts, 1 + the views drawn live with an enabled filter) and `kept: { pictures, mb, retakes, evicted, refused }` (`evicted`, `refused`: the budget's evictions and refused takes in the last second, a refusal that holds counted once).
- Why a view is drawn live (agent builds): `app.renderer.sync.debug.why()` answers `WhyEntry[]` in draw order, one per view with an enabled filter: `{ view, mode: "kept" | "direct" | "live", reason: WhyLive | null, calmIn, retake: { why: RetakeWhy, by } | null }`; every other build a frozen `[]`. `frames().passes.restart` indexes the root export `CANVAS_RESTARTS` (`"none"`, `"first"`, `"filter"`, `"mask"`, `"depth"`, `"empty"`, append-only: why a canvas pass began, WebGPU); a spike's `passes[].restart` carries the name, no key for `"none"`. Root types `CanvasRestart`, `WhyEntry`, `WhyLive`, `RetakeWhy`.
- Filter inputs: `inputs: { blur: { stages: [FrostBox4, FrostGauss], chain: (value, { resolution }) => [{ stage, scale, uniforms? }] } }` gives the body `sampleBlur(uv)` in both languages: the last texture of a chain of stages (each a `defineFilter`, drawing alone) drawn from the view's input into pooled textures at `resolution × scale`. The chain runs only when a uniform or the resolution changed; a step naming a stage not in `stages` breaks the filter. The engine counts the passes (leave `passes` out). `fallback: OtherFilter` (a subset of the uniforms) draws when the filter is broken.
- Shader checks run in every build: every body, stage and fallback compiles once on the device when the renderer first draws, and the first scene mounts after the checks (`effects:mount-waited`). A broken filter (`effects:broken` with reason `compile`, `apply` or `chain`) draws its fallback or the view unfiltered, never a blank frame; a dev build also draws magenta stripes over it.
- Built-in filters: `Glow`, `Outline`, `Blur`, `ColorMatrix`, `Noise`, `Displacement` (`map` is an asset key), `Alpha`. A motion hook tweens them like any component: `view.tween(Glow, { strength: 0 }, { ms: 200 })`.
- API: `app.effects.stats()` returns `{ particles, emitters, filters, renderPasses }`; headless every number is 0.
- `app.effects.diagnostics`: `kinds()` (built-ins, then feature filters, after start), `disable(kind)`, `enable(kind)`, `disabled()` (the off kinds in registration order). A switch acts on a dev or agent page only and answers `false` elsewhere or for an unknown kind (`effects:diagnostics-unknown`, once per id); an off kind keeps its instances and is left out of what the renderer draws from the next frame (`stats().filters` stays, `renderPasses` drops); a switch logs `effects:diagnostics` and writes a `switch` event to the performance log.
- Config: `maxParticles: 3000` and `maxPasses: 24`, each warns once per crossing; `phone: "auto"`; `blur: { quality: 2, phoneResolution: 0.5 }`.
- With `emitters: "fx.starsBurst" | "fx.steam"` in the `defineGame` types, the `defineEmitter` id and `Emitter.effect` are checked by the compiler; `textures` and `Displacement.map` are checked against the asset keys. No events. Depends on `flow`, `world`, `renderer`, `assets`, `anim`.

### platform (V6, Standard, opt-in)

The phone as a provider, last in the array: `plugins: [...screen, effectsPlugin, audioPlugin, platformPlugin]` with `pluginConfigs: { platform: { provider, keepAwake: true } }`. `game.screen()` composes it and takes the provider as its `platform` seam. A game imports no native package: the engine page builds the provider from the `system` list of `config.ts` through `@moku-labs/game/app/system`, and turns keep-awake on when the list names `keepAwake`. The full reference is `src/plugins/platform/README.md`.
- `PlatformProvider` has six members: `onPause(fn)`, `onResume(fn)`, `onBack(fn)` (each returns its remover), `haptic(kind)`, `keepAwake(on)`, `exit()`. Pause and resume push and pop the `"background"` reason of `lifecycle`. A provider method that throws is logged, never thrown into the frame.
- Back chain, `app.platform.back(): BackResult`. First an Escape press: a popup with an `escape` button closes, `"popup"`. Then `flow.gate.answer({ intent: "back" })` when the resting node lists `back`, `"intent"`. Then `provider.exit()`, `"exit"`. Without a provider `"none"`.
- `app.platform.exit()`: the last step of the Back chain alone, `provider.exit()`, for a Leave button: `ctx.require(flowPlugin).fx.handle("exit", () => ctx.require(platformPlugin).exit())`. A throw is logged; without a provider it does nothing.
- Haptics: `await fx(haptic("success"))` in a node, or `haptic("light")` as a timeline step. The kinds are `HAPTIC_KINDS`: `light`, `medium`, `heavy`, `selection`, `success`, `warning`, `error`. A fast walk is silent.
- Config: `provider: undefined`, which leaves the plugin inert: a `haptic` effect resolves at once, so the same node runs on the web and headless. `keepAwake: false`.
- No events. Depends on `lifecycle`, `flow`, `input`.

## Game plugins and events

A game plugin is `createPlugin(name, { depends: [flowPlugin], hooks: ctx => ({ "flow:edge": payload => { ... } }) })`. The root README has the full example in its Events section.

A plugin that owns a resource stores it in its state and frees it in `onStop: ({ state }) => …` (core 1.6: `onStop` receives `{ global, config, state }`). A throwing `onStop` makes `app.stop()` reject. A hook that throws never stops the game: the engine writes the error entry `"game: a hook failed"` to the log (`app.log.trace()`), through the framework `onError(error, core)` of core 1.7. A game can pass its own `onError: (error, ctx) => …` to `createApp`; the kernel calls both.

## Doors for the editor

Two subpaths, neither on the root (V4). An editor, MCP tools and e2e scripts reach a running game through them; `docs/doors.md` in the engine repository has the full catalogue.

- `@moku-labs/game/inspect`: `read(app, source, input?)` reads once; `watch(app, source, input, fn)` reads on the `signals` phase when the source changes and returns the stop function; `defineSource`; the frozen catalogue `sources`; the types `Source`, `InputSchema`, `InputOf`. Every source only reads, so the door is safe in a production build. Keys of `sources`: `graph`, `position`, `history`, `tainted`, `cheats`, `model`, `entities`, `projections`, `ui`, `locate`, `render`, `sounds`, `audioMuted`, `effects`, `filters`, `assets`, `log`, `explain`, `diff`, `schema`, `at`; their ids are `game.<key>`. `filters` answers `{ kinds, off }` of `effects.diagnostics`. `locate` takes `{ key }` (a ui element) or `{ target }` (a view by projection key) and answers its box in CSS px, the numbers Playwright clicks. `at` takes `{ x, y }` in CSS px and lists the views under that point, topmost first. `explain` takes `{ entity }` and answers that entity in full, `undefined` for a stale id. `diff` takes `{ from, to }` frames and answers what changed per entity; it throws in a production build and for a frame outside the last 120. `schema` lists every component and tag type the world met, with the JSON kind of each field. `audioMuted` answers whether the master bus is muted. `sounds` throws `[game] The source game.sounds needs audioPlugin.`, `audioMuted` throws `[game] The source game.audioMuted needs audioPlugin.` and `effects` and `filters` throw `[game] The source game.effects needs effectsPlugin.` (`game.filters` for `filters`) when that plugin is not installed; the editor lists such a source as not installed.
- `@moku-labs/game/control`: `run(app, command, input?)` resolves `{ value, state }`, `state` being `{ path, frame, tainted }`; `defineCommand`; `controlRefused`; `controlReadOnly`; the frozen catalogue `commands`; the types `Command`, `ChoiceInput`, `Ran`, `ControlReadOnlyError`. Keys of `commands`: `answer`, `tap`, `drag`, `key`, `fill`, `scroll`, `walk`, `bookmark`, `restore`, `saveExport`, `saveImport`, `step`, `pause`, `resume`, `capture`, `debug`, `reducedMotion`, `timeScale`, `frameRate`, `mute`, `trace`, `filter`. `capture` resolves `{ png }`, and `{ png, legend }` with `legend: true`; `undefined` while the renderer is inert. `timeScale` takes `{ scale }`; 0 freezes game time while the frames keep running. `frameRate` takes `{ fps? }`, calls `time.setRate(fps ?? "auto")` and answers `time.rate()`. `mute` takes `{ muted }`, mutes the master bus and answers the flag. Without `audioPlugin` it throws `[game] The command game.mute needs audioPlugin.` `trace` takes `{ path }`, a list of views by projection key, and answers whether the gate took the answer. `scroll` takes `{ key, to }`, calls `ui.scroll(key, to)` and answers what it answers; a visual test writes it as the step `{ scroll: { key, to } }`. `filter` takes `{ kind, on }`, switches the filter kind through `effects.diagnostics` (cosmetic) and answers the off kinds; an unknown kind throws `[game] No filter kind "fx.nope".` naming the known ones; without `effectsPlugin` it throws `[game] The command game.filter needs effectsPlugin.`
- Commands run in dev builds and debug builds. `__MOKU_GAME_DEV__ === true` (the dev page, a test's `vi.stubGlobal("__MOKU_GAME_DEV__", true)`) or `__MOKU_GAME_CONTROL__ === true` (`--debug`) runs every command; `__MOKU_GAME_AGENT__ === true` alone (`--debug=read`) runs the `read` and `cosmetic` ones and `run` refuses the others with `controlReadOnly(id)`, an error with `reason: "read-only"`: `[game] The command game.tap changes the game: this debug build runs read and cosmetic commands only.`; no flag: `run` throws `[game] Control commands run in dev builds only.` `moku-game build` defines the three flags `false`; a game without the shell uses a bundler `define` and should add `__MOKU_GAME_AGENT__: "false"` and `__MOKU_GAME_CONTROL__: "false"`. `saveExport` answers the committed `{ player, session, rng }` (read); `saveImport` takes `{ save }` of `saveExport`, restores it at the main flow's start and flushes the store (raw: not on a `--debug=read` page).
- A command's effect is `read`, `route`, `cosmetic`, `cheat` or `raw`. A `cheat` or `raw` command taints the session and is journaled; read it with `sources.tainted` and `sources.cheats`. Of the base commands `restore` and `saveImport` are `raw`; `capture` with `diff` writes the state too, so a `--debug=read` page refuses it. `bookmark` answers `flow.bookmark()` plus `scene`, the mounted scene; `restore` calls `scenes.expect(scene)` before `flow.restore`, so a bookmark at a popup restores the scene under it, also on a page that shows another scene. A bookmark taken while an effect that takes answers waits names the waiting transit node (`info/show` in the mini game) and carries `rest`; `restore` of it answers once that node's gate is open, with `pending.gate` in its value, and the popup shows on the next frame.
- A game's own: `defineSource({ id, title, input, changes, read })` with `changes` `"frame"`, `"commit"` or `"edge"`, and `defineCommand({ id, title, input, effect, run, overlay?, value?, choices?, choice? })`: `overlay: "toggle"` (input exactly `{ on: "boolean" }` and `value: app => boolean`, the switch's state; with `choices: readonly [string, ...string[]]`, each word once or `defineCommand` throws, the input is exactly `{ on: "boolean", choice: "string" | "string?" }` and `choice: app => string` answers the marked one, run with `{ on, choice }`) or `overlay: "button"` (no required input, no value) lists the command in the editor's overlay, which shows only such commands; any other combination is a type error. The id is camelCase words joined by dots, at least two: `dice.rolls`. An input schema maps field names to `"string"`, `"number"`, `"boolean"` or `"json"`; a trailing `?` makes one optional. A command body starts with `if (typeof __MOKU_GAME_DEV__ === "undefined" || !__MOKU_GAME_DEV__) throw controlRefused();`: it runs in dev and is refused on a debug page. A `.dev` command meant for a debug page writes the agent form for a read or cosmetic effect, `if ((typeof __MOKU_GAME_DEV__ === "undefined" || !__MOKU_GAME_DEV__) && (typeof __MOKU_GAME_AGENT__ === "undefined" || !__MOKU_GAME_AGENT__)) throw controlRefused();`, and the control form (`__MOKU_GAME_CONTROL__` in place of `__MOKU_GAME_AGENT__`) for the others. Keep them in `.dev` modules that only the dev page, a debug page and the tests import: the editor's dev page (`preparePage` with agents) and `moku-game build --debug` import every `**/*.dev.ts`, `moku-game build` none.

## Project index

`@moku-labs/game/project` maps every engine id of a game to anchors (a path plus a binding, a key or a component), never to line numbers; `find` reads the line from the file on disk at the call. `typescript` (`>=5.5`) is an optional peer: a game that uses the index adds it as a dev dependency. Nothing is persisted. The contract is in `docs/project-index.md`.

```ts
import { openProject } from "@moku-labs/game/project";

const project = await openProject({ root: "tests/fixtures/mini-game" });
(await project.find("node:infoPopup/count"))[0]?.line; // 7, in "nodes/count.ts"
const stop = project.watch((index, change) => refresh(index.revision, change.moved));
stop();
project.close();
```

- `openProject({ root, manifest?, tsconfig?, debounceMs? })` resolves `ProjectApi`: `index` (frozen, replaced per batch), `find(key)` (a `Found[]`: the anchor plus `line`, `range` `[startLine, startCol, endLine, endCol]` 1-based with an exclusive end column, `hash`, and `broken: true` when the file does not parse now), `watch(onIndex)` (one call per batch that changed bytes, with `(index, change)`; returns the stop function), `changed(path)` (re-index one root-relative path now, no watch call), `close()`. Without `typescript` it rejects with `[game] The project index needs the "typescript" package.`
- Aliases: the index follows imports through the `compilerOptions.paths` of `tsconfig.json` at the root (or the root-relative `tsconfig`), `extends` included, as TypeScript does, so `@core/kit`, `@shared` and `@features/home` reach their files, and `@features/episodes/ep01` the door of a sub-feature. `index.tsconfig` names that file when it holds `paths`. `@moku-labs/game` stays a package. A tsconfig edit rebuilds the aliases in the next watch batch.
- Keys: `flow:<id>`, `node:<flow>/<node>` (every entry of a `nodes` table: node, sub-flow, slot), `feature:<id>` (at any depth; a feature made by a factory has no `feature:` key, its folder is in `features`), `scene:<id>`, `projection:<name>`, `system:<name>`, `emitter:<id>`, `textStyle:<key>`, `style:<path>#<binding>` (a module-level `const` of `defineStyle`), `style:<path>#<function>` (every `defineStyle` call inside a module-level function or function-valued const; `find` answers each call) and `style:<path>#<function>.<property>` (a call under an object property there; a style in a class, an object const or at module scope stays unresolved), `component:<Name>` (in a `.tsx` file a module-level upper-case `function Name` or function-valued `const Name`; anywhere `defineComponent("Name", …)`, bound to its const; `uses` are the files that render `<binding>`), `jsx:<key>`. Definers are recognised by binding from the kit's `defineGame()` destructure, renamed imports too. A non-literal id goes to `index.unresolved` with the reason, never guessed.
- JSX keys are patterns: literal text stays, same-file consts and functions are followed, a key-carrying prop (`id`, or a name that ends in `Key`) becomes a hole of its name, `props.id` reads `{id}` and `props.amountKey` reads `{amountKey}`, any other hole `*`. `` key={`${id}Picture`} `` reads `jsx:card*Picture` (stem `card`); `id="settingsBoard"` on `<Signboard>` reads `jsx:settingsBoard` (kind `idProp`, component `Signboard`, prop `id`); `amountKey="giftReward"` on `<Amount>` reads `jsx:giftReward` (prop `amountKey`). `find("jsx:settingsBoardClose")`, a key `game.locate` reports, answers the `{id}Close` pattern of the kit and the `id=` prop that fills it; a hole takes only the props of its own name.
- `index.features` holds every feature by name, its folder and, for a sub-feature, its parent: `{ ep01: { dir: "features/episodes/ep01", parent: "episodes" }, home: { dir: "features/home" } }`. The feature owners and the code-only sub-features a door lists are in it; a folder that becomes or stops being a sub-feature rebuilds the index and its name is in `change.features`.
- `ProjectChange` is `{ revision, files, moved: [{ key, from, to }], removed, features? }`. A broken file keeps its last good keys and gets `files[path].state === "broken"`. Paths are root-relative POSIX; a path that leaves the root is refused.
- CLI: `moku-game-index --root <dir> where <key>` prints `<path>:<line>` per place (exit 1 for an unknown key); `--json` prints the index; `--check` exits 1 on a broken file or a key in conflict and lists the unresolved items as info. With a tsconfig, `--check` also prints the aliases line, `aliases: tsconfig.json, 8 patterns`, or `aliases: none (no tsconfig paths)`. `--root` is required, `--manifest <path>` and `--tsconfig <path>` are root-relative.

## Hot swap

Dev only. A save of a view file swaps the module in the running page: same state, same node, no reload. `moku-game dev` lists the plugin first in its `.moku/bunfig.toml` and runs the server in the game root, so a game sets nothing; `moku-game build` never loads it. A game with a server of its own lists it in its own `bunfig.toml`:

```toml
[serve.static]
plugins = ["@moku-labs/game/hot"]
```

- View files swap: `.tsx`, `styles.ts`, `view.ts`, `animations.ts`, `effects.ts`, `generated/strings.<locale>.ts` and a sub-feature's `generated/strings.<feature>.<locale>.ts` (while its bundle is not loaded the new module waits for the next load). On the layered layout also any `.ts` directly in a kind folder: `styles/`, `motion/`, `effects/`, `views/`, `world/projections/`, `world/layout/`, in a feature or in `shared/`. Styles, components, function components, projections of a registered name, animations, text styles, emitters and strings. Under `moku-game dev` or the editor's `watchKeys` a save of a strings JSON compiles by itself and its output swaps, a new key too. A game with a server of its own runs `bun run assets:keys` after a strings JSON edit; its output is what swaps.
- Logic files reload the page: `rules/`, `nodes/`, `flows/`, `state.ts`, `tables.ts`, `kit.ts`, a feature `index.ts`, `world/components/`, `world/systems/`. A view file that exports a scene, system, ECS component, filter, flow, node, feature, plugin, a new projection or a new animation is refused: `ui` logs `ui:hot-refused` and throws, and Bun reloads the page.
- Asset files, under `moku-game dev` on the raw files or the editor's `watchKeys`: a texture, a bitmap font (`.fnt` or its page) or a sound saved with new bytes swaps in the loaded bundles, same key, no reload. The keys watch writes `.moku/assets-stamp.ts` `{ files, changed }`, the hot plugin lets the page accept it, and `assets` reads the changed files again. An asset file of a sub-feature swaps the same way. A new, removed or renamed asset file, a changed nine-slice tag too, reloads the page. So does a replace that fails. Not with `--packed`, not in a built game. A bundle that is not loaded reads the new bytes on its next load. A sound that is playing plays on; a running particle effect of a replaced texture starts again.
- A swap logs `ui:hot-swap` and emits the global event `ui:hot-swap` `{ file, module }`. `effects` hooks it for emitters, `assets` for the stamp module.
- Event `assets:replaced` `{ bundle, keys }`, dev only: `assets` emits it once per bundle after an asset swap. `keys` are the asset keys with new bytes; `app.assets.texture(key)`, `font(key)` and `audio(key)` answer the new object and the old textures are destroyed. `text`, `effects` and `audio` hook it; a game plugin that built something from a key hooks it with `depends: [assetsPlugin]` and builds it again.
- Another layout, on a server of the game's own: `export default hot({ include, exclude })` from the game's `hot.ts`, listed as `plugins = ["./hot.ts"]`.
- Keep a view helper in the module of the projection that uses it. A function another module stored into an object at load time keeps the old version.

## Fonts

The package ships one MSDF body font: `fonts/font-body.fnt` and `fonts/font-body.png` (Pangolin Regular) with `fonts/LICENSE.txt` (SIL Open Font License 1.1). Copy it into the game; a path in `node_modules` is not an asset key, the scanner reads keys only from the `assets/` of every feature owner (a feature, or a sub-feature) and of the layers of `--layer`. The licence goes next to `assets/`, not inside it.

```bash
mkdir -p src/features/ui/assets
cp node_modules/@moku-labs/game/fonts/font-body.* src/features/ui/assets/
cp node_modules/@moku-labs/game/fonts/LICENSE.txt src/features/ui/LICENSE-fonts.txt
bun run assets:keys
```

The scanner keys it `ui.font-body`, which is the `text` config default `fonts.body`, so the built-in style `body` works with no config. No `digits` font ships: a game that uses the style `digits` brings `ui.font-digits` itself.

## Testing entry

Exports of `@moku-labs/game/testing`: `createHeadless`, `runRepro`, `stepFrames`, `fakeClock`, `memory`, `saveOf`, `isolate`, `stub`, `fakeFx`. `fakeFx(options?)` is the `fx` of a node context for a unit test that calls `node.run?.({ ...context, fx: fake.fx })`: it returns `{ fx, awaited, started, emitted }`, `options.answer(descriptor)` gives what an awaited effect resolves with, and `fx.start` refuses `answers` and a `guide` as the game does. The visual tests `defineVisualTest`, `runVisualTests`, `parseVisualArgv` come from `@moku-labs/game/visual`, node and bun only (see `docs/testing.md` in the engine repository).

- `createHeadless(app): Promise<HeadlessGame>`. Pass an app that is not started. It sets mode `"fast"`, awaits `app.start()`, starts `flow.run()` unless the app's `onStart` already did, and resolves when the loop rests for the first time: `game.state().path` already names the first rest node. A fatal error of `run()` rejects the call.
- `HeadlessGame`: `walk(route): Promise<FlowState>`, `answer(answer): boolean`, `state()`, `history()`, `stop()`. `walk` and `stop` throw a fatal error of the loop again when the headless runner owns `run()`.
- `Flow.RouteStep` is `{ at: string; intent: string; payload?: Json }` or `{ at: string; result: { outcome: string; payload?: Json } }`. `at` is the path of a rest node. The `result` form substitutes the result of a sub-flow at that path.
- `runRepro(app, { player, session?, rng?, checkpoint?, route }): Promise<{ path: string[]; player; session }>`. The app keeps running. Stop it with `app.stop()`.
- `stepFrames(app, count, deltaMs)` calls `app.time.step(deltaMs)` `count` times.
- `fakeClock(start = 0)`: a `ClockSource` with `advance(ms)` and `set(moment)`. `advance` fires due timers synchronously.
- `memory(fixture?)`: in-memory `PlayerStateProvider` with `calls`, the list of every call. It applies the patches it is committed to the document it holds, so a second app over the same instance reads what the first one wrote. `saveOf(player, seed = 1)` builds a `SaveDoc`.

```ts
import type { Flow } from "@moku-labs/game";
import { createHeadless } from "@moku-labs/game/testing";
import { expect, it } from "vitest";
import game from "./index";

const rollOnce: Flow.RouteStep = { at: "home", intent: "roll" };

it("plays two rolls without a screen", async () => {
  const { app } = game.headless({ seed: 42 });
  const run = await createHeadless(app);

  const state = await run.walk([rollOnce, rollOnce]);

  expect(state.path).toBe("home");
  expect(app.model.store.snapshot().session).toEqual({ rolls: 2 });

  await run.stop();
});
```

Isolated feature tests play one feature without the rest of the game:

- `isolate(feature, options): (seams?) => App`. It composes `options.shared` and the feature as `logicOnly`, then `options.plugins`. The feature's `flow` becomes the node `as` (default `flow.id`) of a harness main flow `isolated`, so paths read as in the game. Options: `flow`, `player` (both required), `as?`, `shared?`, `stubs?`, `plugins?`, `session?` (`{}`), `seed?` (`1`). The factory takes the seams of one app, `player`, `session`, `seed`, `clock`; they win over the options. Pass the app to `createHeadless`.
- `stub(outcome, payload?)`: `stub("closed")` is `{ kind: "stub", outcome: "closed" }`. `stubs: { <node name>: stub(...) }` replaces that node or sub-flow of `flow`; it ends at once with the outcome.
- A node that is not stubbed runs for real, the flow of another feature too.
- A stub is a sub-flow, so a route may still substitute it for one visit: `{ at: "board/energy", result: { outcome: "watch" } }`.
- A checkpoint compacts `history()`: assert on `state()` or on `flow:edge` events.
- Every exit of a flow with outcomes lands on the rest node `exited`; `{ at: "exited", intent: "again" }` enters the flow once more.
- A wrong stub key or outcome does not compile, and throws at run time: `[game] isolate: no node "enrgy" in flow "board".`
- The app's `model.store.snapshot()` is typed by the `player` and `session` of the call, inferred, as `game.headless()` types it: `snapshot().player.count` is a `number`, no cast. A `Model.Json` player reads `Model.Json`.

```ts
import { createHeadless, isolate, stub } from "@moku-labs/game/testing";
import { homeFeature } from "./features/home";
import { mainFlow } from "./flows/main";

// The mini game: home opens the popup info, here stubbed with its outcome ok.
const homeOnly = isolate(homeFeature, { flow: mainFlow, stubs: { info: stub("ok") }, player: { count: 0 } });
const game = await createHeadless(homeOnly());

game.state().path; // "main/home": the harness holds the flow under its id
await game.walk([{ at: "main/home", intent: "info" }]); // the stub ends with ok at once
game.state().path; // "main/home"
await game.stop();
```

For timers, take the clock of `game.headless()`, a `fakeClock(startMoment)`: call `clock.advance(ms)`, then yield the microtask queue before reading the state. The seed is the definition's, else 42; `game.headless({ seed: 7 })` pins another. The headless app composes `logicOnly` of `headless.features`. An app made with `createApp` by hand passes `clock: { source: fakeClock(1_000_000) }`, `model: { seed: 42 }` and `plugins: [feature.logicOnly]` itself; with sub-features it passes the flattened tree, `plugins: flattenFeatures([homeFeature.logicOnly, episodesFeature.logicOnly])` (the `logicOnly` is taken before flattening: a parent's carries its children's).

## File layout of a game

```
index.ts          export default defineGameApp({ ... }): the game as one data object
config.ts         export default { page, native?, system?, save?, assets? } satisfies GameConfig
core/             the kit (the defineGame call) and its types
shared/           the shared layer
features/<f>/     one feature: flow/, rules/, views/, styles/, motion/, world/, assets/, strings/
features/<f>/<sub>/   a sub-feature: index.ts, assets/ or assets.ts or strings/, and the kind folders
plugins/         the game's own plugins
generated/        what moku-game keys writes: assets.ts, the strings, manifest.json
tests/            the tests; tests/scenarios/<name>.ts are the saves of ?player=<name>
.moku/            what moku-game writes, ignored by git
```

Rules are pure functions in `rules/`: no engine import, no clock, no random. The tsconfig aliases are `@core/*`, `@shared`, `@features/*` (`@features/episodes/ep01` reaches a sub-feature). The lint rules `layer-imports`, `feature-door` and `test-suffix`, the hot kind folders, the `assets.layers` of `config.ts` and the project index follow the layers `core/`, `shared/`, `features/` and `plugins/`.

The worked example is the merge game in moku-labs/demos (https://github.com/moku-labs/demos), written on the public API only, with its e2e and visual tests. The engine repository keeps a smaller fixture, `tests/fixtures/mini-game/` (`index.ts`, `config.ts`, `tests/scenarios/ready.ts`, one rest node, one popup flow, two features), and `tests/fixtures/episodes-game/`, a game on the layered layout with a parent feature `episodes` and the sub-features `episodes-kit`, `ep01` and `ep02`; neither is in the npm package. A feature with a screen adds `view.tsx` (projections and components), `animations.ts` and `strings/<locale>.json`. Each plugin has a README: `src/plugins/<name>/README.md` for `time`, `lifecycle`, `model`, `clock`, `flow`, `world`, `renderer`, `input`, `assets`, `scenes`, `anim`, `i18n`, `text`, `ui`, `audio`, `effects`, `platform`. Moku Core specification: https://github.com/moku-labs/core/tree/main/specification
